title: The Baristro Asian Style
address: The Baristro Asian Style สุเทพ, 200 Suthep Rd, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
This place is huge and features a beautiful Japanese-style garden. It was super crowded when I visited, likely because it coincided with the Chiang Mai University graduation. The crowd was a mix of teenagers and office workers, so it was quite bustling and not very peaceful. Luckily, my group managed to find a seat just in time!

There is an 80 THB entrance fee, but you can use the ticket as a discount for food and drinks inside.

The prices are standard for a cafe, and everything tasted good. The staff were friendly and provided great service. Since it was so busy, the drinks were served in order, so you might have to wait a bit. Overall, a lovely spot—just be prepared for the crowd on busy days!

user_reviews.Description: Delicious coffee. I just finished taking my Professional Barista level course (not certified yet but on my way to do so).  If you are looking for Chiang Mai grown coffee this is one of the cool places for that. The Dirty Coffee is a must try to order when you are there. Also if you want a souvenir to take home or give as gifts you can buy their 250 g bags, especially the Wan Wan (toffee caramel stone fruit) medium roast which goes well for cold and hot coffee (see my picture). Remember to look at the roasting date, very important to consume within 3 months from that date to get very good quality coffee. Enjoy it.

user_reviews.Description:
A café with a wide range of creative menu items, and everything tastes great. The space is large, with a raw loft-style, industrial vibe. There are multiple seating zones on both the first and second floors, and several restrooms available.

The highlight is the outdoor seating area by the Ping River—perfect for relaxing and enjoying the view, especially when the weather isn’t too hot. You can easily sit and chill there for hours. I really like it.

The café offers a variety of drinks, bakery items, and food. The coffee is good, and I also tried another drink (can’t recall the name) that had a nicely balanced blend of flavors. The lemon cake was slightly on the dry side, but the ham & cheese croissant is a must-try—highly recommended, it’s delicious.

There’s parking available in front of the café. You can order at the counter and choose your seat freely. The staff are friendly and provide great service.

user_reviews.Description:
The Baristro x Ping River is a masterclass in blending industrial design with the natural serenity of Chiang Mai’s riverfront. From the moment you step inside, the raw concrete walls and minimalist wooden accents create an atmosphere that feels both modern and incredibly welcoming. The expansive glass windows offer a stunning view of the Ping River, making it the perfect sanctuary to escape the heat of the city. I found the ambiance to be truly exceptional, especially with the way the sunlight filters through the space during the afternoon.
The coffee here is clearly handled with expert precision, showcasing a depth of flavor that only a dedicated roastery can achieve. Whether you prefer a bold espresso or a creamy latte, the quality of the beans shines through in every single sip. However, the true standout of the visit had to be the tiramisu, which was executed to perfection. It struck the ideal balance between the bitterness of the coffee-soaked layers and the airy sweetness of the mascarpone cream. Every bite was indulgent without being overwhelming, making it one of the best desserts I’ve had in the region. Between the scenic riverside seating and the high-end menu, it is easily a highlight of the Chiang Mai cafe scene. It is the kind of place where you can lose track of time just watching the water flow while enjoying a world-class treat. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone who appreciates great design as much as they do a professional-grade brew.

user_reviews.Description:
We have been here twice now and there are so many good things about this cafe - it is definitely in my top 2 favorite cafes in Chiang Mai!

1) FOOD: all the beverages & snacks we ate so far have been YUMMY. I esp like the soft latte (like a light latte with ice cream & whipped cream) & absolutely LOVE their scones with clotted cream & jam. The scone is a small cute little pastry, paired with a real clotted cream (like from a real tea service, not just butter.)

2) SERVICE: their staff work very quickly & efficiently to bring you what you ordered by using the tabletop number signage, there are many people working to deliver orders & clear tables, and most importantly the staff are friendly, helpful, & customer service oriented. For example, we had a little snafu or misunderstanding with our order (which was easily just as much our fault with our communication!) but they were so apologetic & accommodating in trying to make up for the misunderstanding, even when we insisted we were the ones who made a mistake while ordering! Then they tried to refund some of our money! (We did not take it & insisted they please put it in their tip box!) Lovely!

3) ATMOSPHERE: the view & ambiance are lovely - scenic water, lush trees, many indoor & outdoor areas, plus a variety of seating options- lounge chairs, couches, arm chairs, tables & chairs in a quiet room if you want a work space, etc. (Plus, many of the staff were willing to help take photos since many of their seats are scenic with a view!)

HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PLACE! 👍

title: KRISP Café
address: 35, KRISP Café, Siritron Alley, Chang Phueak, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50300

user_reviews.Description:
Krisp Café is such a beautiful and peaceful spot.
I ordered the pistachio raspberry croissant, and it was absolutely delicious—perfectly flaky, warm, and rich with buttery layers. The raspberry tasted fresh and added just the right balance without being too sweet. The combination was surprisingly perfect.
I also had a caramel macchiato, which was smooth and well-balanced. No complaints at all.
The best part is the atmosphere. The space is calm, beautifully designed, and offers both open seating and quiet corners if you just want to relax or think. I could easily see myself hosting a small event here or simply coming back for a quiet moment alone.
Highly recommend if you’re in Chiang Mai.

Krisp feels like a hidden gem tucked away in a small alley.
It’s a café with a wide variety of desserts, along with a dedicated baking area.

The Coconut Americano and Dirty were both good and up to standard.
The Chocolate Matcha Lava was especially delicious—the lava combines chocolate and matcha, though the matcha flavor is a bit subtle. Still, it’s well-balanced overall.

The café has three floors, with seating zones uniquely designed on each level. Outside, there’s an old swimming pool repurposed as a photo spot for customers.

The staff are friendly and provide great service. Parking is available along nearby streets.

user_reviews.Description:
Roastery Coffee, Chiang Mai

A must-visit for coffee lovers in Chiang Mai! Here’s why:

* 🏆 The baristas are exceptionally skilled, and it’s home to a World Champion Latte Art barista, making every cup feel extra special.
* 😊 The service is warm, friendly, and professional. The staff are happy to answer questions and recommend drinks based on your preferences.
* ☕ The coffee is outstanding, with beautifully crafted espresso drinks and excellent bean quality. Definitely one of the top specialty coffee spots in Chiang Mai.
* 🌿 The café has a comfortable and inviting atmosphere—perfect for relaxing, catching up with friends, or simply enjoying a great cup of coffee.
* 📍 Conveniently located in the heart of the Nimman area, just about a 5-minute walk from One Nimman, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighbourhood.
* 🚕 Parking can be limited, so I would recommend taking Grab for a hassle-free visit.

If you’re serious about specialty coffee or simply want to experience one of Chiang Mai’s best cafés, Roastery Coffee is definitely worth adding to your itinerary.

user_reviews.Description:
I’ve been to 7 Senses Gelato many times, and it’s one of those places that I always find myself coming back to. 🍨 The shop offers a wide selection of flavors, from classic options to creative seasonal ones. Every time I visit, I try to discover a new favorite, though I have to admit that most of the flavors are quite sweet for my personal taste since I don’t eat much sugar. However, my company — whether my friend or boyfriend — always enjoys them a lot, so it’s a great spot to share something sweet together.

The shop provides free drinking water, which I find very thoughtful, especially after eating gelato. The staff are a bit shy but always kind, polite, and ready to help. The atmosphere is peaceful and quiet, perfect for sitting down to enjoy a slow afternoon in Chiang Mai.

The location is convenient but not ideal for car parking since the street is quite small; however, it’s easy to park a motorbike nearby. I usually order one or two scoops each visit.

Overall, it’s a charming little gelato shop that serves great flavors with a friendly vibe. Definitely recommended!

user_reviews.Description:
The indoor area is quite small. If there's a large group of customers, you're most likely going to need to take turns playing with the cats.

And if you happen to arrive at a time when the cats are all sleeping, well, then, probably best just spend time playing some board games provided for free.

None of the cats I observed were curious with the humans, except when they're bribed with food (not kibbles laying on their regular bowls). 90% were sleeping, or hiding away at a corner. Most are ok with petting, but they mostly mind their own business and dgaf about visitors (I suppose they've grown weary of strangers and just acted naturally?)

Also, with the small space and some 10+ cats, there's bound to be a smell. Those that claim there's no smell probably have been living with cats all along, or spent more than 30+ mins inside. It's pronounced when one just steps into it and the smell will integrate with your senses once you're in it long enough. The smell is not that bad though.

The drinks are a little expensive, but they don't charge any other fees so it's reasonable.

I just found it rather boring tbh.

user_reviews.Description:
KLAY Café is such a beautiful hidden gem in Chiang Mai. The moment you step in, you’ll feel the calm, minimalist vibe — warm wood tones, natural textures, soft lighting, and thoughtful interior design that makes the whole space feel cozy yet modern. It’s the kind of café where you just naturally slow down and enjoy your meal.

We tried a few dishes and everything was beautifully plated and full of flavour:

Smoked Salmon & Eggs Toast
The toast was soft and buttery, topped with generous slices of fresh salmon and perfectly runny eggs. The mix of pickles, tomatoes, and passionfruit on the side added a bright, refreshing balance. Loved how satisfying yet light it was.

Thai Beef Salad
A colourful bowl with tender slices of beef, sweet oranges, juicy tomatoes, red onions, and a nice kick from fresh chili. It’s refreshing with a nice balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy — great for brunch or a hot day.

Besides the food, the café also has a small curated retail corner with skincare and lifestyle products, adding a boutique feel to the place. It’s a lovely spot for brunch, a slow afternoon coffee, or even just to chill and enjoy the aesthetic environment.

Overall, KLAY Café is definitely worth a visit if you’re in Chiang Mai — delicious food, beautiful ambience, and a very inviting atmosphere.

title: Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store
address: 24, Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store, 9 Nimmanhaemin Soi 17, Suthep, Muang, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
If you’re serious about coffee, Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store is a must-visit in Chiang Mai. This place completely lived up to the hype for us. From the moment you walk in, you can tell coffee is taken very seriously here — the space feels modern, stylish, and almost like a specialty coffee lab rather than just a café.

The coffee itself was incredible. Smooth, rich, perfectly balanced, and easily some of the best coffee we had in Thailand. You can really tell why Roast8ry has become internationally known in the coffee world, especially with their award-winning baristas and latte art. Watching the drinks being made honestly felt like part of the experience itself. (Food & Wine)

We also loved the atmosphere. The dark modern interior, the smell of freshly roasted beans, the music, and the overall energy made it somewhere we genuinely wanted to stay for a while instead of just grabbing a coffee and leaving. It felt trendy without trying too hard.

It’s located in the Nimman area which is already one of the best neighborhoods in Chiang Mai for cafés and restaurants, so it fits perfectly into a café hopping day around the city. Prices are definitely higher than local Thai coffee shops, but for the quality and experience, it was absolutely worth it.

If you enjoy specialty coffee even a little bit, Roast8ry Flagship Store is one of those places in Chiang Mai that you should not skip.

title: Carp Café
address: 118 Nong Kwai, Hang Dong District, Chiang Mai 50230

user_reviews.Description:
Delicous food, great service and fantastic vibes!

The food was great. It was very well made, came quickly and tasted just like it was supposed to. Both drinks and food were very profesionally made. It was a little but pricey compared to other places, but it's a very touristy place and there's a lot of upkeep with the fish, so it's understandable.

The service was terrific! We were serviced quickly and when ready to order they came immediately. The waiters were very kind, patient and seemed happy to be at work.

And of course, the venue! It was so cool with all the fish, and the seats were inside of the pool, under waterlevel, so that you could easily see, feed and interact with the hundreds of fishes there. Ask for fish food and you will get 2 choices; normal fish food or a baby bottle so you can feed them like a baby.

The whole experience was really fun and I recommend you try it when you're in town 😄

You can feed the fish by purchasing fish pellets and fish milk provided by the café. One of the highlights is the uniquely designed toilet area filled with koi fish — it’s definitely something you should check out when you visit.

The whole place is surrounded by countless koi carp, some of them absolutely huge, swimming right around the seating areas. The café itself shows a little bit of age in a few places, but that really doesn’t matter – you come here for the experience, and that is fantastic.

user_reviews.Description:
One of the most memorable specialty coffee experiences I've had.
I ordered a V60 brewed with locally grown Thai beans from Chiang Rai. The coffee itself was excellent—clean, sweet, well-balanced, with delicate floral and fruity notes—but what really impressed me was the attention to detail.

The coffee was served in a wine glass with a lid to preserve the aroma, alongside a handwritten brew card showing all the extraction parameters: brew ratio, dose, water temperature, brew time, TDS, and even the expected flavor profile. It felt less like ordering a cup of coffee and more like a personalized tasting experience.

You can tell the team genuinely cares about every step of the process, from sourcing the beans to the final presentation. If you enjoy specialty coffee, MoR is absolutely worth a visit.

title: PIMM'S CUP : Roastory Lab
address: Samlarn Rd Old City Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
We are always on the lookout for great coffee and authenticity. You definitely can find that here. I’ve had a lot of coffee in my life but this is the first time I’ve had farm to table.

Pim, the owner and farmer, happened to be in the shop and made two wonderful coffees for us. Despite her costs doubling over the last few years she’s kept her ristretto, espresso and doppio at 50 THB.

If you’re into coffee, you have to give the place a try. Btw, there is a great wine bar, Cru, across the street.

Pim recommended visiting the nearby night market as well as Wat Phra Singh to catch the sunset behind the gold stupa.

title: Cafe Arte
address: Cafe Arte 155/4 หมู่ 2 ถ.เจ็ดยอด-อยู่เย็น ซ.8 Chang Phueak, เมือง Chiang Mai 50300

complete_address.street: 155/4 หมู่ 2 ถ.เจ็ดยอด-อยู่เย็น ซ.8

user_reviews.Description: I stayed here for 10 nights and chose it mostly because its located at a walking distance from the Night Bazaar, the Wat Chedi Luang (a 10 to 15 min. walk to both) and because of the price - it was quite hard to find a non-shared room for less than USD 15, especially an a/c one, very much needed in Chiang Mai.||I got the Superior Room - No Balcony, but upgraded to the one with balcony for less than a couple dollars per night. They gave me a discount because I had a long stay here. Both rooms are small indeed, but I found them comfortable enough. There's a double bed with a firm-but-comfortable mattress, nice pillows and comforter, a small bedside table, cable flat screen TV, and two 0.5L complimentary bottles of water per night. The bathroom is also small but it's not cramped. The water is hot (you can adjust the temperature), the water pressure is good and the towels are big. The a/c works pretty well.||The staff is friendly and kind. Their youngest "staff, Minah, is such a pretty, well behaved and cute little girl! It's a very homey feeling you get here. They provide laundry service at 40 baht/kg and will clean the room upon request. There's indeed a lot of mosquitoes, but I suppose you can just ask for a bug spray. I managed to kill the ones in my room on the first night and didn't get any more uninvited visitors. There's no elevator here and the rooms are located on the 3rd and 4th floor. I also got a 1h foot scrub with massage for THB 350 and it was very good. The sir who did it has a very firm grip, which I prefer and not only my foot and calf are soft and smooth, but the calf pain I was feeling after so much walking is gone!||There's plenty of B&Bs and restaurants on the street where F.K. House is located to have meals. I recommend Da's Home Bakery for their Mixed fruit with Muesli and Yogurt, Addy's Happy Smoothies for their Iced Thai Milk Tea and Iced Coffee Milk, and Lucky Too for their pizzas.||Right on the corner it's Somphet Fresh Food market where, apart from fruit and vegetables, you can buy BBQed meat and fish, small trays of sliced fruits (10 to 20 baht), fruit shakes (40 baht) and some souvenirs - good to have an idea of starting prices before going to the other famous markets. Within 100m you can find a Tesco Lotus Express, a 7-Eleven, ATM, drugstores and local restaurants. I recommend Grazie Thai, I had so many meals there and the dishes are very tasty! I also tried Aroy Dee but for me it was just okay.||For the price, comfort, and location, I'd say it's a great deal!

title: FOHHIDE
address: 14/2 ชั้น 5 Nimmana Haeminda Rd Lane 5 Nimmanhaemin Tambon Su Thep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

complete_address.street: 14/2 ชั้น 5 Nimmana Haeminda Rd Lane 5

user_reviews.Description:
Nestled on the top floor of the building, away from the bustling streets of Nimman, is FOHHIDE. They have a good variety of coffee drinks and mixes, which is nice, but what the place truly delivers is the experience that comes with it.

The view looks directly towards Doi Suthep, over the rooftops of Nimman, with planes flying by; all from the comfort of an air-conditioned café. In fact, on a good day where clouds are thinner, you may even spot Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.

Best of all, they accept Apple Pay/card and mobile payments without any extra charge (as I write this), and the coffee is pretty well priced. I found myself coming back multiple times over the next few days.

FOHHIDE is truly a hidden gem, tucked away on a building in the heart of Nimmanhaemin. It’s a small, charming café where you can enjoy a great view of Chiang Mai city. The staff are friendly and welcoming.

The café offers drinks and bakery items, and most of the seating is bar-style—either at the counter or at the bar facing the view. The coffee is excellent.

There are both indoor and outdoor seating areas. The outdoor section is especially popular, as many people come there to take photos. It’s definitely a must-visit spot to check in when you’re in Chiang Mai.

Sincerely wish this lovely family‑owned restaurant ongoing prosperity. I truly encourage travellers to come and experience its heart‑warming charm for themselves.

title: Lot of Taste
address: 8 Lot of Taste, 5 Nimmanahaeminda Road Nimmanhaemin Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
Lot of Taste, better known as L.O.T., is a specialty coffee café in Chiang Mai's Nimman area. Designed with a minimalist blend of exposed concrete and warm wood, the space feels open, bright, and relaxing thanks to the abundance of natural light. Rather than being a café built purely for Instagram, it is a place where people come to enjoy good coffee. One of its highlights is the variety of coffee beans available, along with its signature drinks featuring Soft Cream, which gives the café a unique identity beyond a typical latte.

When I visited, the café was quite busy with a mix of locals, tourists, and expats. Some were working on their laptops while others were catching up with friends, yet the atmosphere remained calm and comfortable.

Here's what I tried:

Hot Latte
The café uses its own house blend, combining beans from Doi Chang and Lator Gold. The result is a balanced cup with smooth milk, gentle acidity, low bitterness, a creamy texture, and subtle caramel sweetness. It's easy to drink and well-rounded without being overpowering.

Soft Latte
This is the café's signature drink and one that many people come specifically to try. Instead of traditional milk foam, it's topped with a thick layer of Soft Cream, similar in texture to soft serve, sitting on an iced latte. Each spoonful gives you both coffee and cream together. The Soft Cream is silky and lightly sweet—lighter than whipped cream and far less sugary than ice cream. It's worth tasting the cream on its own first before gently stirring it into the coffee, as the flavor gradually changes from the first sip to the last.

Tiramisu
The tiramisu has a light, airy texture with just the right amount of sweetness. It pairs naturally with coffee without feeling too rich, and melts smoothly in your mouth.

If you're exploring Nimman and looking for a comfortable place to relax with a well-made cup of coffee and a slice of dessert, Lot of Taste is definitely a café worth adding to your list.

Visited this lovely café at One Nimman and had a great experience! Here are my thoughts:

At a higher-end price in Chiang Mai, this does not meet the cut.

강바람 맞으면서 고양이 쓰다듬을 수 있는 평화로운 카페입니다. 🌿🐱

The scenery here is absolutely beautiful, making it the perfect place to relax and enjoy some peaceful time looking out over the Ping River. Even though there is no air conditioning, the natural river breeze keeps the place pleasantly cool.

The lychee tea in my photo not only looks beautiful but tastes amazing. The honey lemon tea I had the day before was also delicious, and they even refilled it with hot water. They serve decent meals and desserts like Basque cheesecake. There is a Halal sign, so dishes like Pad Kra Pao are available only with chicken or beef. There are also lovely resident cats here, and you can buy cat treats for 20 THB to feed them. Free Wi-Fi is available as well.

I would absolutely love to come back here the next time I visit Chiang Mai. Thank you for such a wonderful experience! 🙏✨

user_reviews.Description:
Cocoa Latte 70 ฿ (2026)

Has English menu.

A hidden gem!!

Just look at the view, and the greens in the cafe, they are so relaxing and beautiful.

The owner/staff very friendly and smiling. It gives good vibe.

There are many different types of seating and the design is very good as not cramp so it won’t get noisy.

And the Ping river is the main protagonist, peaceful, calm, murky.

And the sun, best supporting actor of all time, shining thru the trees on my seat, on the river, making it glistening from time to time.

And best cameo goes to occasional boat passing by, making ripples, just like witnessing time passing in slow motion and dance right in front of my eyes.

I stare at it for the longest time, while enjoying my coffee, didn’t realize time passing in un relative sense.

I had my AirPod on, with Debussy playing for me, this could be one of the best moment that I need to remember how wonderful to be alive.

I am just another ordinary human, quietly living, but I awed at my blessing, the beauty of my surroundings.

The feeling is wonderful.

And I wish you could feel that too.

user_reviews.Description:
Such a nice little café tucked away from the crowds it’s a perfect spot if you’re looking to escape the hustle and bustle for a bit. The location feels calm and minimalistic, with very chill background music that makes it easy to relax and enjoy your time.

The cappuccino with oat milk was the real highlight for me. Creamy, smooth, and absolutely delicious this was easily the kind of coffee I’d come back for again. The croissant was served warm and nicely flaky, exactly how it should be.

I also tried the coconut matcha, which was really well balanced, not too sweet and not too bitter, making it very enjoyable. The only downside for me was the signature lemon cake. It wasn’t as spongy as I expected and leaned a bit dry and too sweet for my taste. Not terrible, just not my favorite.

Overall, a great spot for a quality cappuccino with oat milk and a peaceful atmosphere. Definitely worth stopping by if you want good coffee in a calm, tucked-away setting.

title: Somewhere Espresso Coffee Roaster
address: 63/3 Loi Kroh Rd, Tambon Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50100

user_reviews.Description:
This is my favorite little “hidden gem” coffee shop in Chiang Mai. Super-friendly owners, amazing coffee and non-coffee drinks (their Thai iced tea was one of the best I had in Thailand), and some tasty pastries to go along with it!  They sell some fantastic local beans as well, which I can highly recommend. For the quality, it’s amazing how reasonable the prices are.

When the weather is moderate they open up the front of the shop to be open-air, but during the heat of the afternoon they close it to keep it nice and cool inside with air conditioning. Very convenient location to grab-and-go, but they have a surprising large amount of seating for such a tiny little place: 2-3 benches/tables inside, as well as 3 tables outside. Really recommend for a getting a drink and people-watching for a wee bit outside.

Edit (August 2025): Was back in Chiang Mai and wanted to stop in again. The shop has changed a bit and become better! They had added a much larger indoor seating area (you can comfortably sit with your drink), and they also have a list of single origin and house blend coffee beans you can choose from to have as a pour-over or in your coffee drink of choice. I am adding the pictures below to show these changes. They’ve also got a few more creative coffee concoction, as well as some desserts (cookies and cheesecake) to choose from. The couple who own this place are still lovely, and the woman’s English is excellent for talking about coffee, so if you have any questions please feel free to ask! I cannot recommend this spot highly enough - in a city filled with awesome coffee shops, this one is my favorite.

Update (May 2026). It just keeps getting better and better. More indoor space, more seating, more selection of beans and also matcha as well. Coffee is still roasted on-site and is fantastic black or with milk. This is still my favorite coffee shop in the city, and definitely the best place to pick up some great arabica beans to take home. Come enjoy!

user_reviews.Description:
12 Feb Homey Café is a peaceful, beautifully designed spot in Chiang Mai.

The building is calm and minimalist, with a Japanese feel: a stone path through raked gravel, a neat green lawn and a simple house with floor-to-ceiling windows. Inside, light wood, soft white curtains and comfortable chairs make it bright and relaxing, with garden views from every table.

We had the yogurt bowls, topped with fresh orange, banana, apple, grapes, blueberries and granola, served with honey and extra toppings on the side. The thick toast came with butter and a lovely homemade orange marmalade, and the Thai iced tea was a good match. Simple, fresh and nicely presented, with real attention to detail.

A perfect place for a slow breakfast, a quiet coffee or a few hours of reading. Highly recommended.

user_reviews.Description:
intensely into drip coffee,  per much of the new coffee culture here. Ordering a drip coffee here is having a voyeuristic adventure.  They don't do big brew baskets/pots of coffee . Drip coffee means a personalized, experienced, individual coffee. Every step of the process, which u r invited to see upclose is meticulously crafted and cured . Weighed carefully, ground by hand grinder, sniffed for perfection, poured in cool genie bottle glass (similar to ChemEx), then poured back n forth from different glasses to achieve maximum taste by not letting it get too hot.  It was amazing . Coffee was too 😄.   They only do light roast or similar of course. Max flavor profiles.  Notice the light hue of the coffee.
The whole place is like a retro flappers era bar, cool music ,  odd statue carving stores in the back through the narrow hall.
Lots of hip Thai young people there.
Highly recommend for coffee snobs. They take coffee extremely serious . (Discourage milk or cream ofc, but they'll give u milk if u want on the side).
And also , see how they make iced coffee !! They pour hot pour over into a bowl of ice 🧊!😮, which is apparently popular here

user_reviews.Description:
Tucked within One Nimman, GRAPH Coffee is such a delightful spot to unwind. The environment is beautiful—cozy, stylish, and very inviting. It’s the kind of place where you can easily lose track of time just enjoying the atmosphere.

What really stands out is their extensive selection of coffee mocktails. These are not your usual drinks—each one is a unique and creative blend, mixing coffee with unexpected flavors. Truly impressive and exciting for any coffee lover.

We ordered the Downtown, and wow, it was incredibly refreshing and tasted soooo good! Perfect for the summer heat. Honestly, it was so addictive I was tempted to go for a second cup immediately.

My friend had the Jungle, which leans towards a more earthy profile, paired with their signature soda mix. A really interesting and exotic take on coffee—great for those who enjoy something a little different.

The croffle was another highlight—crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and absolutely satisfying as a light bite. They also offer a good selection of pastries if you’re looking for something to go along with your drinks.

Overall, a fantastic experience with great drinks, cozy vibes, and creative offerings.
Highly recommended!

title: The Story 106 Co-Working Space &Cafe
address: 200 Tha Phae Road, Tambon Chang Moi, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50300

user_reviews.Description:
A beautiful hidden gem and one of those places where you can easily lose track of time. This boutique café has a cozy, peaceful atmosphere with lots of character. The upstairs area is especially calm and quiet, making it a great spot to get some work done, read, or simply relax with a good cup of coffee.

What makes the place unique is the beautiful collection of handcrafted wooden items throughout the boutique, from chopsticks and ladles to photo frames and decorative pieces. The interior and wall décor add even more charm, while the large windows offer a lovely view—especially on a rainy afternoon. ☕️🌧️

The coffee is excellent, with espresso-based drinks made using beans ranging from light to dark roasts. I tried the Thai local medium roast, which had a smooth, medium body with pleasant nutty notes. The pastries and desserts are also worth trying—the banana croffle and mango sticky rice were beautifully presented and delicious.

Overall, it’s a wonderful place to spend a couple of hours browsing the handcrafted items, enjoying coffee and pastries, or getting some work done in a peaceful setting. Highly recommended! ☕️✨

user_reviews.Description:
Some places serve great coffee and cake. Others leave you with a beautiful memory. TORA BAKE somehow manages to do both. ❤️

I genuinely had such a wonderful time here. The food and drinks were delicious, and I especially recommend the chocolate mint cake! Everything feels carefully made, with love and attention to detail. I also really appreciate their eco-friendly, zero-waste philosophy. It's lovely to see a small business that genuinely cares about these things.

The café itself is peaceful, cozy and welcoming. Whether you want to read a book, enjoy a coffee, get some work done or rent a dedicated workspace, it's a wonderful little escape from the busy city.

But what truly makes TORA BAKE special is Ice, the owner.

What an incredibly kind, warm and genuine person. We had such a lovely conversation, and honestly, that human connection was the highlight of my visit. She has this beautiful way of making you feel welcome, not just as a customer, but as a person. You can find good coffee, delicious cakes and coworking spaces in many places in Chiang Mai, but the warmth and positive energy Ice brings to this little café are something you simply can't replicate.

As a traveler, these are the moments I value most. Sometimes you walk into a place expecting nothing more than a nice drink, and you leave with a smile, a meaningful conversation and a memory you'll carry with you.

Thank you, Ice, for your kindness, your beautiful energy and for making my time here so special. I wish you and TORA BAKE all the success and happiness you deserve! ❤️

If you're visiting Chiang Mai, please don't miss this little gem. And when you go, make sure to say hello to Ice for me! 😊

I'll definitely remember this place long after leaving Chiang Mai. Will be back for sure Ice :)

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a peaceful and high-quality coffee experience in Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Description:
We visited Blue Coffee on 24 June. It was an oasis after we had visited several temples throughout the Chiang Mai old city, and it's right across the street from Wat Srikird.

They have a large selection of drinks available, and a fine display of cakes and other sweets. They have AC, and a cool industrial feel on the inside.

We ordered a Blue Latte and a Cold Brew Cream. They were both really good, and probably worth the total cost of 210 Baht, which is the most we've paid for coffee in the area.

The staff was friendly, and brought our drinks to our table when they were ready. Overall it was a good experience, and we would be happy to return.

user_reviews.Description:
150 baht per person to enter and it comes with a free drink. There is a place to hang up your bags and they ask that you either bring socks, or tell provide you with a pair of you can buy snacks for the kitties, too.

There has to be like 20 cats in this cafe. It was soooo clean, and the cats are so cute and friendly. When you order a drink, it comes with a cover on it so no fur gets in. Fur is everywhere haha. They let you hold them, you just need to be sitting down. They have two floors, and there are cats everywhere you look. This was such a fun time, you get to stay for two hours. Right outside is a little market, there’s a restaurant and there’s a cafe and juice shop as well. They even had live music when we arrived.

If you bring a car, you can park for 50 baht. I’d recommend coming not only to the cat cafe, but check out the vendors, the food and art stores around as well. A cute little gem, hidden and tucked away. Definitely a great place to bring family if they’re visiting.

user_reviews.Description:
A cozy Cat Cafe,  just 5 mins walk from art village Baan Kang Wat.  Visitors need to wash hands and wear socks before getting inside.  THB 150 per person for a 2-hour session with a nice drink.  Staff informed us some rules about how to get along well with cats such as hanging up bags, put lids on our drinks, and no holding cats moving around, etc.  We can see how they take care of visitors and cats by setting up clear rules.
There are over 20 friendly cats napping or enjoying their time around.  After a while sitting quietly with them, a few may approach you and even jump on your thigh purring.
As a cat lover, I love this place and definitely will come again next time when we visit Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Description:
Late January 2026 Local Hmong cafe serving a wide range of specialty and crafted coffee ☕️

One of the few interesting places at the village originated when the peoples of this region once cultivated opium poppy plantations.  The then late king made efforts to introduce more sustainable alternative crops and soon a small coffee industry was born.

The selection itself is notable from basic blends to single origin beans 🫘 reflecting the deep knowledge of the family behind this local brand.  Even selective beans are available as well as various brewing options.

The staff is strictly counter style with option to do your own pour 🫗 over order.  Retails options are also available as well as other coffee by products and alternative drinks.  Meals pairings are also at hand.

The atmosphere and the view are particularly beautiful and once can imagine the restful view in the early sunrises 🌅 😍 👌   Truly one of the must visit places in the village.

user_reviews.Description:
Visited with a large group of friends and ordered several drinks, desserts, and ice cream. Overall, the café is lovely, the atmosphere is great, and the matcha was absolutely delicious.

The only issue we experienced was with the service. One of our drinks was ordered hot but was served cold. When we politely informed the staff, we were told that we had not specified that we wanted it hot. However, the person who placed the order had actually asked which drinks could be served hot before ordering, so we were quite confident that the request had been made.

What was disappointing was not the mistake itself, as errors can happen anywhere, but the response and attitude we received. The staff member seemed visibly annoyed and unwilling to acknowledge that there may have been a misunderstanding.

Thankfully, another staff member stepped in and kindly said, “No problem, we’ll fix it for you,” and resolved the issue right away. We really appreciated her professionalism and helpful attitude.

Mistakes happen, especially when a café is busy, but I believe maintaining a positive attitude and listening to customers carefully is just as important as serving great food and drinks.

Despite this experience, we still enjoyed our visit. The matcha was excellent, the desserts were lovely, and the café itself is beautiful. I hope the team can improve the consistency of their customer service, as the café has so much potential

user_reviews.Description:
I almost didn’t post this review since I don’t want to blow up this spot, but after going here multiple times within the two weeks we were in Chiang Mai, I felt like it was my duty to share how magical this place is.

As someone who drinks matcha everyday at home I was craving  quality matcha spot and kohicha is quite literally the best matcha experience I’ve had. Their menu has a wide variety of strains with tasting notes listed as well as a guide to which ones make for good lattes and which are best drank just with water. Oat milk swap is free and there are other alt milk options!

All the staff is really knowledgeable and have great recommendations.

The wifi is great for working and there are a few larger tables and outlets. It does get busy so these spots are not always guaranteed. It’s also a dog friendly location which has been a welcome distraction in my experience.

I’d also highly recommend the daifuku strawberry mochi. I get it every time! The chocolate cake is also phenomenal. The Nutty Yama has been my favorite so far out of the ~10 I’ve tried but it’s also a limited edition option.

Bring cash as card is not accepted.

user_reviews.Description:
Serene Backyard is a beautiful little nook surrounded by greens right in the center of Chiang Mai. Offering riverside dining and lounging, the hosts provide a very warm and caring atmosphere that makes you want to extend your stay from lunch until dinner time and beyond. They have a great variety of food and drinks that cater to many different tastes. Live music bars are within walking distance and according to the staff there will be concerts at the Serene Backyard in the near future too. No need to change locations if you’re that type of person. All in one well done. Love finding these gems. Hats off to the new team. Keep it up! Cheers

PS: Can't speak for the rooms yet besides the looks, but the accommodation definitely caters to the ones who stay up til closing time anyway as the rooms are more or less above the main area. You just gotta walk up a set of stairs and can go to bed.

user_reviews.Description:
We were really lucky to meet Mook, the owner of this lovely place, and to have a deep conversation about her vision, and passion towards her small business, and the values behind Mood:D (which I fully share). We were enjoying to talk with her so much that we nearly forgot to eat our food. No joking, I think we have spoken for an hour without a single pause. 😅
If you’re looking not only for a place with outstanding food and drinks quality but also for a place to have a rest, to calmly work, to chat with nice people, - I would 100 percent recommend Mood:D.
Dear Mook, thank you for your hospitality! I wish you all the best and hope to see you again one day.

It would be really cool if they had some windows show casing the ping river.

user_reviews.Description:
visited the café with a friend and it was such a beautiful experience. The café is a bit far from the city center (around 5 km), but it’s absolutely worth the trip. The place is peaceful, charming, and surrounded by nature. At times, it felt like being in an Alice in Wonderland garden, with rabbits hopping around, ducks, and even pigs nearby.
There were very few people when we visited (day week around 4pm) which made the atmosphere even more special. It’s the perfect spot to disconnect, read, write, or simply relax, with the sound of the river flowing in the background.
The service was incredibly kind and attentive. We shared a two-tier basket of pastries with fruit. The portions are small, more like tasting samples, but the flavors were outstandin, delicate and absolutely delicious.

I forgot to ask for my cappuccino without sugar, and the staff was so kind that they prepared a new one for me without charging for the first cappuccino at all ❤. That gesture really stood out.

Overall, the place is beautiful, calm, and full of charm. I highly recommend visiting for the pastries and for a quiet, relaxing afternoon surrounded by nature.

Service and experience: 10/10.

user_reviews.Description:
We took a taxi all the way to Transit Number 8 because it was highly recommended online and had good Google ratings.

Big mistake.

The security guard at the entrance refused to let us in unless we bought vouchers first  60 THB per person. We politely asked if we could at least walk in and look around before deciding, but the answer was no.

The funny part? We were not even driving into the parking area. We arrived by taxi and were simply walking in.

It was hot, we were tired and thirsty, and instead of welcoming customers, this place treated us like a problem before we even stepped inside.

I have never seen a café force people to buy vouchers just to enter. We came for coffee, not attitude.

Luckily, only five minutes away we found Blue Coffee, which had better drinks, a better atmosphere, and most importantly, normal human hospitality. I’ll attach photos from there instead.

Don’t let high ratings fool you. Good coffee means nothing when the first thing customers experience is arrogance at the gate.

title: Blink me Bunny Cafe&Bistro
address: Blink me Bunny Cafe&Bistro แม่ปิงวิลล่า Tambon Don Kaeo, Mae Rim District, Chiang Mai 50180

complete_address.street: แม่ปิงวิลล่า

user_reviews.Description:
We stopped here for brunch on our way to the Land Department, and it turned out to be a pleasant experience.

The café is set amidst beautiful Thai countryside and feels like a mini zoo. Inside, there's air-conditioned seating with two friendly cats that are curious and playful. Outside, you'll find teepee-style seating, where you can enjoy your meal alongside mini goats, a deer, and a small stream filled with koi fish. The toilets were clean, the staff were attentive and prompt, and there was ample parking.

One thing I appreciated most was that the animals—including the tortoises, rabbits, pigs, deer, and cats—looked healthy and well cared for. That's always important to me when visiting places like this.

Food was decent!

A word of caution: while the mini goats look cute, they become quite aggressive when they see the fish food. I was charged twice by the goats. Because of that experience, I would strongly advise parents to keep toddlers very close, as a child could easily be knocked over.

Overall, it's a lovely stop for families with young children or anyone looking for a picturesque, nature-filled setting. My child isn't little anymore, and I'm not on Instagram, but we still enjoyed the peaceful surroundings and had a fun visit as it wasnt crowded at 11.

user_reviews.Description:
We were out exploring various places alongside the Ping River north of Chiang Mai City when we came across this completely unexpected and outrageous cafe, the "Blink Me Bunny Cafe‘ & Bistro."

It has a large garden area alongside the Ping River and houses various animals such as ducks, geese, cats, goats and deers.  The animals are very friendly and amusing to watch.  Ideal amusement for families and children.

We had coffees and cakes which were good, and just a little on the expensive side.  The only thing we didn't like about this place is the payment system where you have to photograph a q code and look at the menu on your phone.  We hate this as it's not nearly as efficient as providing a hard copy menu.

Other than that, a brilliant place to have found and highly recommended for an amusing change.

Plenty of dining areas inside and out.

user_reviews.Description:
Fern Forest Cafe is a hidden tropical oasis right in the heart of Chiang Mai's Old City. The moment you step through the entrance, you are greeted by a lush canopy of ferns and mature trees that make you feel like you’ve wandered into a secret garden. I absolutely loved the ambiance, which strikes a perfect balance between a tranquil forest setting and the vintage elegance of a colonial-style white wooden house. Whether you sit outside by the koi pond and small waterfall or inside near the grand piano, the atmosphere is incredibly peaceful and restorative.
The coffee here is equally impressive, served with a level of care that complements the serene surroundings perfectly. Every cup feels like a craft experience, providing the ideal caffeine kick to accompany a slow morning or a mid-day break from temple-hopping. However, the real star of the table for me was the tiramisu, which was rich, creamy, and expertly layered. The balance of the bold espresso-soaked sponge against the light mascarpone was divine, making it easily one of the best versions I’ve tried in the city. Between the chirping birds and the dappled sunlight filtering through the leaves, the entire dining experience felt like a scene from a fairytale. It is the kind of place where the service is as warm as the sunshine, making you feel immediately at home. I would highly recommend Fern Forest Cafe to anyone looking for high-quality brews and desserts served in a beautiful, shaded sanctuary. It is truly a must-visit destination for those who appreciate great food paired with a stunning natural environment.

title: Fleur Cafe & Eatery
address: Tung Lung Soi 4, Mae Raem, Mae Rim District, Chiang Mai 50180

user_reviews.Description:
Absolutely beautiful place with great food and especially great drinks, but a bit weird arrangement and heavy focus on photo taking.

This seems to be essentially two separate restaurants. One is a full service restaurant, but we were seated away from all the flowers with a view on the waiters checking their phones. Another is a small cafe with just cakes and coffee and other drinks (no alcohol) where you can take out the food and sit in the beautiful, stunning surroundings.

The house wine was unexpectedly really good. A blueberry milk-based drink was amazing too. Smoked salmon bagel looked amazing in the photo but the bread tasted a little bit burned — still enjoyed it though. Service varies; some people seem clueless and disinterested, and some others speak perfect English and ask whether you enjoyed the food and are happy to introduce what's available.

One small note: I would really love to have proper thick paper napkins instead of the toilet paper style tissues, to protect clothes from getting stained.

Plenty of space for car parking. Absolutely worth visiting with kids. Prices are fine given the setting and quality.

title: Akha Ama Coffee ( The New Original )
address: moonmueang soi 9 Old City Tambon Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
If you’re wandering around Chiang Mai looking for a caffeine epiphany, Akha Ama Coffee is exactly where you need to drop your baht.
Let’s talk about the undisputed star of the show: the Dirty Latte. At a glorious 100 baht, it shines bright and mighty! I’ll confess, it’s my runner-up favorite in the city (Twenty Mar’s still holds the crown at 150 baht, but they bribe me with double the volume and a cheeky side of two chestnuts—hard to beat). Still, Akha Ama's dirty latte is an absolute powerhouse of flavor that demands respect.
Then there’s the wild card: the Orange Juice with Coffee. I know, it sounds like an accidental morning spill, but it is a surprisingly good combination! It’s the citrusy, caffeinated plot twist my tastebuds didn't know they needed.
Fair warning: the space is tiny, and snagging a seat can feel like a competitive sport. My go-to cozy nook is at the backmost area just past the restroom, which is great, but comes with a caveat. You will absolutely hear the constant chit-chat of the staff (they always seem to have a surplus of them hovering around) paired with the unmistakable acoustic stylings of a random customer peeing in the restroom.
If you prefer your espresso without a side of gossip and bathroom sound effects, make a break for the second floor. If you’re lucky and the place isn't packed to the brim, you can score some solemn, glorious quiet up there to sip in absolute peace.

Must go for cat lovers. 🐾✨

user_reviews.Description:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Magokoro Teahouse is one of the most beautiful and unique spots I visited in Chiang Mai.

The moment you walk in, it genuinely feels like stepping into a piece of Japan. The wooden interiors, garden views, and overall atmosphere are calm and thoughtfully designed. Sitting by the window looking out onto the greenery is something special, especially as the light changes throughout the day.

The menu is extensive, with a wide range of hot and cold teas, including traditional tea ceremony options. There’s also a great selection of matcha at different price points depending on quality, which is a nice touch. I had an iced matcha latte with almond milk, and being able to choose sweetness level and milk alternatives made it feel really tailored.

I also tried the Lumiere chocolate dessert, which was excellent and paired perfectly with the matcha.

The staff were friendly and welcoming, and when it’s not too busy they let you choose where to sit, whether that’s inside or out in the garden.

I ended up staying for about four hours without even realising. Watching the space transition from bright daytime to a softly lit evening garden was such a nice experience.

I’ll definitely be returning before I leave Chiang Mai. This place is worth slowing down for.

title: The Baristro at Train Station
address: วัดเกตุ, 46/1 Rotfai Alley, Tambon Wat Ket, เมือง, Chiang Mai 50000

complete_address.street: วัดเกตุ, 46/1 Rotfai Alley

user_reviews.Description:
If you're looking for a stylish café near Chiang Mai Railway Station, The Baristro at Train Station is definitely worth a stop. Inspired by the atmosphere of a classic train station, the café features railway tracks at the entrance, station-style signage, and an industrial design with exposed concrete, steel, and grey tones. The overall look feels raw, modern, and surprisingly welcoming.

The café is spacious, with the coffee bar positioned in the center so you can watch the baristas prepare each drink. There are plenty of seating options, whether you're visiting alone to enjoy a quiet coffee or catching up with friends. Large windows let in plenty of natural light, making the space feel bright and comfortable despite its industrial aesthetic. Even though it's a popular café, it never feels too crowded or cramped.

What We Ordered

Soft Latte
A great choice for anyone who enjoys creamy coffee. This latte is topped with a smooth, silky soft cream that adds a rich, velvety texture. Each sip combines the bold flavor of espresso with the light sweetness and creaminess of the topping, creating a well-balanced and enjoyable drink.

Peachino
A refreshing combination of peach, soda, and coffee. The fruity aroma and sparkling soda bring a bright, refreshing start, followed by the deep bitterness of the coffee. The contrast between the sweet peach and the coffee works surprisingly well, making it an excellent choice for a hot day.

Overall, The Baristro at Train Station is more than just a coffee shop. It offers plenty of photo-worthy corners, a wide selection of specialty coffee, non-coffee beverages, and freshly baked pastries. If you're around Chiang Mai Railway Station and looking for a cool place to relax, enjoy a good drink, and capture some industrial-style photos, this café is well worth a visit.

user_reviews.Description:
One of my favorite things about Chiang Mai is that the road up to Suthep always seems to have a surprise waiting. On one of my usual motorbike runs through those cool, forested bends, I stumbled onto Baan Suan Café — and I've been coming back ever since.
The grounds are wonderfully spacious, spread across several buildings with a relaxed, garden-estate feel. If the afternoon heat gets to you, the central air-conditioned building is a welcome retreat. But honestly, I prefer settling into one of the open pavilions with a fan going, listening to the trees and watching the light filter through. It just feels right for the setting.
The food is honest and decent — nothing pretentious, just solid cooking at prices that won't make you think twice. They don't serve alcohol, which actually suits the peaceful atmosphere perfectly. This isn't the place to party; it's the place to slow down.
Whether you're winding down after a ride up the mountain or just looking for somewhere to breathe and eat well away from the city buzz, Baan Suan is genuinely worth the detour. A quiet little reward at the end of a beautiful road.

user_reviews.Description:
I went here randomly since it was close by where I was.

For drinks this place is primarily chocolate-based drinks but they do have some coffee based drinks too. I tried a Dark Chocolate mocha drink and asked the waitress to choose 3 of her favorite praline chocolates for me to try as well.

I wanted to pay by credit card but I was informed that I must spend at least 500 baht to pay by credit card. So she chose 5 more chocolates in order for me to reach 500 baht for everything.

I have to admit It that it is a little annoying that even a very nice place like this they have such a high spend barrier in order to use the credit cards. I could understand if it was a small business that was just starting out but this seems like an upscale business.

Was it all 500 baht good? In my opinion the chocolates all look beautifully crafted but strictly speaking the taste wasn’t worth it for me. I do think for a gift for someone if you want to get some special chocolates this would certainly be an upgrade over regular chocolates though.

My favorite of the 8 was definitely mulled wine followed closely by Black Forrest. Least favorite was the Dark Chocolate and the Pistachio one.

The drink was just okay for me and did not stand out more like the Pralines did so perhaps I chose the wrong drink.

If I were to return I certainly would try a different drink and I think I would get a singular main chocolate dessert than maybe trying more of the cute chocolates.

Praline’s I tried:

Black Forrest -  9/10

Cookie’n Cream 8/10

Dark chocolate - 6/10

Macadamia biscoff - 8/10

Mango sticky rice - 8/10

Mulled Wine - 10/10

Pistachio - 7/10

Yuzu -  8/10

title: Bella Goose Cafe at the Hill
address: 169/4 Sridonchai Rd, Chang Khlan Sub-district, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50102

user_reviews.Description:
Bella Goose Café – A Wonderful Breakfast Experience in Chiang Mai

During my visit to Chiang Mai, I stopped by Bella Goose Café for breakfast, and it quickly became one of my favorite cafés in the city. The café has a cozy, modern atmosphere with plenty of natural light, making it a perfect place to enjoy a relaxing breakfast or brunch. The staff were warm, friendly, and attentive, making me feel welcome from the moment I arrived.

For my meal, I ordered the Chicken Pad Kra Pao with a Fried Egg, a classic Thai favorite. The minced chicken was flavorful, perfectly seasoned with Thai holy basil, garlic, and chili, and served over freshly steamed rice. The crispy fried egg with its runny yolk added the perfect finishing touch, making every bite rich and satisfying.

I also couldn’t resist trying the café’s Signature Waffles. They were freshly made, golden brown, crispy on the outside, and light and fluffy on the inside. Served with syrup, they were a wonderful sweet treat that complemented the savory main course perfectly.

To drink, I chose a Matcha Latte, and it was excellent. The matcha had a rich, earthy flavor without being overly bitter, while the milk created a smooth, creamy texture that balanced everything beautifully. It was refreshing, well-crafted, and paired perfectly with both the waffles and the spicy Pad Kra Pao.

Overall, Bella Goose Café exceeded my expectations. From the delicious food and high-quality drinks to the welcoming service and relaxing atmosphere, every detail made the experience enjoyable. Whether you’re looking for a hearty Thai breakfast, freshly made waffles, or a perfectly prepared Matcha Latte, this café is definitely worth visiting. I highly recommend Bella Goose Café to anyone visiting Chiang Mai, and I’ll certainly be back on my next trip. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

user_reviews.Description:
A fantastic minimalist spot with a great atmosphere, superb workspace vibes, and excellent quality food!

The Setup: Went to carrot coffee in Chiang mai for midday. We found this place via Google maps as we wanted to have a nice coffee and light snack for lunch. We ordered 2 drinks, a ham and cheese toastie, a carrot cake and 2 cake pots, one oreo and one banana.

What stood out:

✅ The Space & Service: As soon as you walk in it's got a minimalist modern industrial style, which I love. To the left when you come in is the counter, got fresh patisseries and cakes. Staff were great and helpful, good English and super attentive.

🔥 The Experience: We sat upstairs and connected to WiFi, which was pretty good to be honest. It's a great place to come and get your work done, or to have a light catch up and chill. All the food was lovely and fresh, cooked to order and baked that day.

🙌 The Value: 9.6/10 - Great spot with good atmosphere and great quality food. Getting fresh, baked-daily food and a productive, aesthetic workspace with solid WiFi makes it highly worth it.

The Verdict: Overall, great spot with good atmosphere and great quality food. I would come back.

user_reviews.Description:
This is hands down the most magical café experience I’ve had in Chiang Mai! I stayed from 9 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon and didn’t want to leave.

The entire property is a sprawling, serene Japanese-style garden with trickling streams, stone waterfalls, manicured greenery, misty bamboo groves, and even a charming red bridge and wooden water wheel. Every corner feels like a scene from a peaceful film, and the atmosphere is incredibly calming and full of natural energy.

The café itself is clean, bright, and quiet, with both indoor and plenty of outdoor seating options. The food and drinks are reasonably priced for such a stunning setting, making it perfect for working, relaxing, or simply losing track of time surrounded by nature.

A true hidden gem in Chiang Mai, 100% worth a visit!

Kindest regards & thank you for the amazing time - Daniel

The atmosphere was incredibly quiet, warm, and peaceful. I was deeply impressed by the coffee expert who looked like a grandfather—or perhaps a father—and by the kind service of his grandson, or maybe his son. My heart felt warm because of them.

On my last day, I said goodbye and told them I hoped we’d meet again next year.
I visit Chiang Mai every year, so it felt a little sad that I only discovered this place now.
At the end of 2026, I’ll go there every day :)
Until then, I wish you good health and happiness.

The carrot cake was genuinely one of the best I’ve had, perfectly moist with cinnamon fragrance, packed with raisins and walnuts and finished with a cream cheese frosting that had just the right balance of sweetness and saltiness. title: Free Bird Cafe CNX Donation Center and Thrift Store
address: 14 ถนนศิริมังมังคลาจารย์ Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, 50200

complete_address.street: 14 ถนนศิริมังมังคลาจารย์

user_reviews.Description:
Free Bird Café is a natural, cruelty free thrift store and plant-based eatery hidden away on a secluded back street. The first time I went for lunch I had the Mac and Cheese which was really nice - the Vegan sauce is something special. I came back for dinner and I gotta say that the Thai Khao Soi is one one the best laksa type soups I've ever had - exceptional!
Unfortunately I found my next dish, the Rainbow Pad Thai to be fairly uninspired. The dish definitely needed a little something extra - such as marinated Tofu for example.

But there are plenty of really cool new takes on traditional Burmese and Shan Vegan dishes on the menu that I look forward to trying in the future 😊

There is a rack or two of second-hand clothes and they also sell handmade crafts.

They have in stock an organic blend of tea called Blue Lotus - I really recommend it to help you wind down after a busy day.

They also have an impressive array of "Herbal Smoke" if that floats your boat.

Oh! And don't forget- 100 Percent of all profits at Free Bird goes towards helping the Burmese refugees so every baht spent goes to a worthy cause. Please donate generously as this money is desperately needed.
🙏❤️

user_reviews.Description:
I ordered the Elwood and my friend had the Holiday. Both were exquisite.

Elwood gives off a very masculine, manly vibe but in coffee style (mixed with Triple sec).

Holiday is essentially a pudding dessert layered with activated charcoal and a bit of milk, so you get that layered taste (bitter in a good way).

What surprised me most was the Elwood. I was expecting it to be smoky and roasty, much like a Negroni’s bold, bitter profile, but it ended up tasting like orange peel without that stinging bitterness, which was unexpectedly good.

user_reviews.Description:
We visited this elephant cafe thinking it was ethical, and I really regret supporting it.
We should have done more research beforehand, but at first it seemed like a place where the elephants could roam freely. Instead, they were kept in designated spots for tourists. After our meal, we bought a fruit basket to feed them and took photos like everyone else.
What made me sick was what I saw afterward. While tourists were distracted feeding the elephants, I noticed two staff members on the side hitting and kicking a baby elephant. Seeing that completely changed everything for me. If this happens while visitors are around, I can’t imagine what happens behind closed doors.
I feel awful knowing my money contributed to this. Please do your research before visiting places that advertise “ethical” elephant experiences. Don’t make the same mistake we did.

Seeing that completely changed everything for me. If this happens while visitors are around, I can’t imagine what happens behind closed doors.
I feel awful knowing my money contributed to this. Please do your research before visiting places that advertise “ethical” elephant experiences. Don’t make the same mistake we did.

title: No.39 Cafe
address: 39, No.39 Cafe, 2, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
Whilst the setting is nice and very picturesque, the charm and character do lack of an independent business. The food is bland, nothing special and albeit over priced. I tried the mango coconut milk moose (I couldn’t tell this was mango apart from the name). I also tried the strawberry New York cheese cake (whilst the strawberries were nothing to write home about- I’m British and when in season our strawberries can be 👌🏼, the biscuit base was soft and watery and I believe this was frozen and defrosted, which is unfortunate). I also had the iced crème brûlée latte (dark + less sugar) which had a good sweet and dark kick, but then became more ‘nothing’ (and I didn’t leave it too long as there was still plenty of ice left in the bottom).
The ‘system’ is poorly ran. There is nothing personal about this place (no waiting on service, which for the price I’d kind of expect). Whilst it is not a a chain shop the automated system isn’t automated, you still have to queue up to be served by a member of staff (seems very pointless). I saw ants in amongst to deserts which did put me off reordering anything when I went to get water. The staff clearing tables are working very hard in the heat, but don’t seem very happy which to me speaks volumes about the management of this place. I’d also suggest having someone regularly checking the toilets, as when I used the facilities there was no way of drying your hands (thankfully the heat sorted that one out!). Personally I wouldn’t recommend making a special journey to come here (as I did), as it currently stands it isn’t worth it. For such a picturesque place it is a real shame.

user_reviews.Description:
If you’re at Baan Kang Wat (market) walk down here for a chance to sit, have a bite and a cold drink.

Pros- lots of space with tables spread out over the shaded area surrounding a strangely blue colored pond or pool. Low volume music playing which was in no way too much. Wide menu choices, desserts as well as drinks.

Confusing start- you enter into a covered hallway like space then go to the side room to place your order.  From there you walk out towards the radioactive colored water feature with a buzzer to find seating.

Cons- The pizza pictured was essentially a roti thin crust with margarita toppings.  We split it as we weren’t very hungry it did seem small.

Curious con- The ongoing obsession with girls getting pictures taken in several hundred poses using the blue water backdrop was non stop.  Not being young, shapely or from this culture it mystifies me.   It becomes free entertainment for dinners so there’s that.

Great variety of mostly western dishes, heavy on the brunch and toast choices. Really well put together. The ingredients were fresh.

I’m on a one meal a day fast so my intake of thick cut bacon on egg toast, wagyu beef skewers and salad with avocado, quinoa/poached egg was perfect. Loved the inclusion of sprouts  to add a bit of earthiness. Eggs were not over cooked but silky, soft and fluffy.

Space was plentiful and a mix of practical tables with some outdoor seating next to moving water. Looks like they have little toys for kids to stay busy while parent eat and lighting and space were in no short supply.

Prices are reasonable for a western menu but the star is the range and variety offered. There are some Thai dishes as well but they have some offerings I’d come back to try like their soft shell crab Benedict or soft shell crab pasta.

title: WTF Coffee Camp

user_reviews.Description:
This is a wonderful place to escape the city and enjoy a relaxing meal surrounded by nature. The highlight is definitely the beautiful waterfall view, which creates a peaceful atmosphere that’s perfect for spending a slow afternoon with family or friends. After lunch, sitting down with a cup of coffee while listening to the sound of the flowing water makes the experience even more enjoyable.

There is an entrance fee of 100 THB per person, but you’ll receive a 50 THB voucher that can be used at either the restaurant or the café, making it feel like a fair deal.

The food was delicious and full of flavor. I especially enjoyed the Khao Soi, which had a rich, creamy curry broth and tender chicken. For drinks, my mom said the hot Caramel Macchiato was one of the best she’s had, while I absolutely loved the Thai milk tea. It was rich, refreshing, and incredibly tasty—I would happily order it again.

The prices are definitely higher than at most local restaurants, but considering the beautiful setting, relaxing atmosphere, and overall experience, I think it’s worth visiting at least once. If you’re looking for a place where you can enjoy good food, quality drinks, and stunning natural scenery all in one stop, this is a destination I would happily recommend.

user_reviews.Description:
We had passed by this cafe several times before finally deciding to stop in, and we’re so glad we did. From the outside it already caught our attention with its unique style, but stepping inside was even better. The atmosphere was super cool and creative—something about the design and interior gave us this futuristic, almost “Mars-like” vibe. It’s definitely not your average coffee shop; every corner feels thoughtfully designed and Instagram-worthy.

We ordered their signature drinks along with coffee, and both were excellent. The flavors were rich and well-balanced, clearly made with care, and the presentation was just as impressive. It’s one of those places where you can tell the drinks are crafted to stand out, not just served.

Beyond the drinks, the overall experience was really enjoyable. The seating was comfortable, the music matched the vibe, and it was the kind of place where you can relax for a while—whether to chat with friends, read a book, or just enjoy the ambiance.

This cafe has such a cool personality that makes it stand out in town. We left already planning to come back again, not only for the great drinks but also for the one-of-a-kind atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re looking for something different and stylish!

We visited Butter Is Better while craving a proper western brunch after weeks of travelling Asia, and it completely exceeded our expectations. The food is excellent value for money and so good that my fiancé and I came back a second time.
There’s a great variety on the menu, everything is freshly made to order and easy to customise. The homemade yoghurt is a must, they serve real butter (not margarine), and the portions are huge (by British standards). The meat in the cooked breakfasts tastes like it’s straight from a local British butcher.
If they had a branch back home, I’d be a regular — highly recommend to any travellers in Chiang Mai looking for an amazing brunch.

The coffee selection is thoughtfully curated, and the space itself — neat, minimal, Japanese in spirit — is genuinely peaceful. Exactly the kind of place you return to without needing a reason.

Shakshuka tasted like canned pasta sauce with some eggs thrown in. They added lots of mushrooms in it without listing mushrooms anywhere on the menu, but I’m allergic to mushrooms. No flavor. Very overpriced. I ordered Turkish eggs initially but they were sold out? The only ingredient difference with the pasta sauce & eggs ‘Shakshuka’ was yoghurt. They’re literally in the same building as a yoghurt place, so how they’re out of yoghurt is a mystery.
Avocado toast lacked any flavor as well. The regular whitecoffee is good, but the special coffee drinks are not. I have no idea why this place has high ratings. Probably the most overpriced and overrated place I’ve been to in 5+ trips to Thailand, dangerous if you have food sensitivities or allergies as ingredients and allergens may be added to any dish without any way to know.

user_reviews.Description:
Our local friend brought us here during our bike ride. For him, this was the original "coffee" shop that made him fall in love with coffee shops in Chiang Mai. Actually, we were supposed to go to another place, but it was  closed, so we came here instead.

I can see why locals come here. There's a sense of calmness about sipping your coffee by the moat, and just letting time past by slowly.

Most of us ordered the Gravity drink, based on the barista's recommendation and it was spot on. Smooth and light, with just the riggt amount of caffeine for my liking. Our other friend ordered the Cocaine drink, and it was also very good.

We will definitely come back here, when we visit Chiang Mai in the future.

user_reviews.Description:
rolled in on a random Chiang Mai morning, left questioning every coffee I’d had before.

Picked a washed Honduras. Dry aroma. Gooseberry and cream. Wet. Ripe apricot — straight up.

Hot sip: apricot flesh wrapped around my whole mouth, finishing like rose tea I didn’t order but desperately needed.

Mid-temp acidity popped off — bright berries, juicy as hell, no weird sharpness.

Low temp turned into smoked plum — round, syrupy, sweet, and stupidly long finish.

My friend’s  ordered the Dirty it tasted like thick velvety. Milk knew its role and nailed it.
This place doesn’t flex. It just delivers. Don’t sleep on Asama.

user_reviews.Description:
Update July 18, 2026–
It is my pleasure to update my review. After a speedy and thoughtful reply from the owner the least I could do was return to Basecamp.

I have returned twice since my initial visit. On both visits, the music reflected the setting of the shop—peaceful, calming and inviting. I enjoyed sitting at the bar height counter staring out into tree line of the jungle.

Besides serving up great coffee, you can also purchase running apparel and gear. In the same location is a running store and places to order food.

Whether you enjoy sitting in the comforts of air conditioning or absorbing fresh air sitting on a deck, Basecamp Coffee Club has a place for you.

Enjoying life, one coffee shop at a time.

- - - - -

I truly want to LOVE this coffee shop. I’ve traveled to over 800 coffee shops in the last three years, and this space has so much potential. But the music — especially the last several songs — has been loud and filled with profanity and sexual content.

The peace you’ve created here is being shattered by the atmosphere the music brings. The setting at the base of the mountains is tranquil, and the environment itself invites people to slow down, breathe, and enjoy the moment. I would love for the music to reflect that same sense of peace.

user_reviews.Description:
There are two cute dogs in this coffee shop(Sometimes they are not in the shop).
I especially like the big brown dog named Taco (It sounds like "Takoyaki" or "Tako( which means octopus in Japanese)" )  because he is very charming and his behaviour and characteristics are really similar to these of my dog.
I took a lot of pictures of him : )
His is like "a beckoning dog" (the original one is a beckoning cat)  as he really made me want to come here.

Customers are also allowed to bring their own dogs so you may have a chance to see other cute dogs.
You can enjoy interacting with dogs without paying additional fee :) though sometimes their dogs are not in the shop.

Their Thai food tastes so good. I think their food has higher quality than other Thai food shops do.
I personally think Thai food is one of the best foods in the world ( though the country may not be the best for me to live in... I am sorry to say this. I still like Thailand as a tourist destination).

user_reviews.Description:
Fringe in Chiang Mai is a total gem! From the moment you walk in, the ambiance hits you with such a cool, inviting energy that makes it hard to leave. The interior design strikes the perfect balance between modern style and cozy comfort.

The food is equally impressive, with every dish tasting incredibly fresh and thoughtfully prepared.

What really sets this place apart, though, is the live music, the performers are talented and create the best vibe for a night out. It’s the kind of spot where the music is soulful enough to enjoy but still allows for great conversation.

The service was also top-notch, with a staff that makes you feel like a regular on your very first visit. Whether you’re there for a full meal or just a few drinks, the experience is consistently five-star.

I honestly can't recommend Fringe enough to anyone visiting Chiang Mai. It is easily one of my new favorite spots in the city, and I already can't wait to go back!

title: CHARLIE (ชาร์ลี) Thai Tea - Nimman Soi13 (Grab&Go)
address: CHARLIE (ชาร์ลี) Thai Tea - Nimman Soi13 (Grab&Go) 2 Nimmana Haeminda Rd Lane 13 Nimmanhaemin Tambon Su Thep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
Came by specifically to try their Thai tea and was genuinely impressed. The quality exceeded expectations, ordered less sweet, with well-balanced flavors that aren’t overly sweet — exactly to our preference. Standout picks were the Charlie (Salted Caramel Cold Foam Pour Over Thai Milk Tea) and the Soft Latte Thai Tea, both smooth, fragrant, and nicely layered. We went with the staff’s recommendations for type of tea and honestly, you can’t go wrong with any of them.

The outlet itself is small and minimal, quite cool inside, with only a handful of chairs available indoors and outdoors. There was no queue when we visited, making it ideal for a quick grab-and-go. Perfect for picking up a drink and strolling around the area. Definitely worth a try if you’re a Thai tea fan. I prefer this outlet compared others.
