user_reviews.Description:
From the moment you step in, this place takes your breath away. It feels like walking into an art gallery that seamlessly blends into nature. Every corner has been thoughtfully designed, with beautiful details that make you stop, look around, and simply say “Wow”

Then you walk out onto the terrace, hear the gentle sound of the stream, and find yourself surrounded by lush greenery. It’s incredibly peaceful and almost feels too beautiful to be real. It’s the kind of place where you could happily spend hours with a coffee, a book, or just your own thoughts.

I’ve visited a couple of times for drinks, and they’ve been excellent every time. I still haven’t had the chance to try the food, but that’s definitely next on my list.

This is one of the most beautiful cafes I’ve ever visited, and a true hidden gem. I already can’t wait to come back! 💚

user_reviews.Description: Discover the most enchanting café in Chiang Mai, nestled just north of the Old Town in the charming Chang Pueak neighborhood. Step into a tranquil oasis where a cascading waterfall, a peaceful pond, and vibrant greenery create the perfect escape from the city’s hustle and bustle. Savor exquisite European-style cakes and pastries, paired with expertly brewed coffee and a variety of fine teas—all at prices friendlier than those in the historic center. What makes this experience truly special? Every visit supports and empowers the local deaf community, making your time here not only delightful but meaningful.

user_reviews.Description:
This is our favorite café to work from with a laptop, we’ve been here several times! It has a fantastic view, plenty of seating options, and excellent coffee and beverages at great prices. Everything you order arrives quickly.

Most of the time, they serve food, and it’s fantastic, but occasionally the kitchen is closed, so it’s worth checking about food availability on the same day.

The outdoor area is absolutely STUNNING! They’ve created a small jungle with a waterfall, and it’s amazing.

What makes this place even more special is that people with hearing disabilities work here and provide wonderful service. The café is also located near a school for children with hearing impairments, which makes their inclusivity even more inspiring.

I wish this place all the best! Thank you for everything!

title: Taste Cafe
address: 2 Chiang Rai Rd, Tambon Su Thep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
I’ve been coming to Taste Cafe for about 8 years now, and I still keep coming back every time I visit Chiang Mai.

It’s one of those places I feel genuinely connected to. The coffee has always been consistent — rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced, just the way I like it. Whether I order my usual favorite or try something new, I’m never disappointed.

The atmosphere is cozy and comfortable, great for relaxing, catching up with friends, or even getting some work done. The staff are friendly and welcoming, which makes the experience even more special.

For me, Taste Cafe is a must-visit spot in Chiang Mai — a place I’ll always return to. ☕

user_reviews.Description:
Fairly crowded on a Sunday morning around 8:45am, but we managed to get a table for two. The crowd continued to build up shortly after.

Food options are limited, though there’s a wide variety of drinks. We tried the classic shiopan and the shiopan with pork and cream cheese. The classic shiopan was dense on the outside, hollow in the middle, and nicely buttery with a hint of salt — enjoyable.

We had a mocha and a latte; both were decent.

The music was a little loud, but overall it’s a pleasant spot to sit, relax, and people-watch.

Note: credit cards are not accepted — payment is via cash or QR only.

user_reviews.Description:
KAME KAFE is a hidden gem for coffee and tea enthusiasts. This cozy café boasts an impressive variety of both beverages, catering to everyone from traditionalists to those seeking unique flavors. The quality of the coffee is exceptional—each cup rich, aromatic, and crafted with care. The tea selection is equally noteworthy, featuring blends that are both comforting and intriguing.

However, parking might be a slight challenge as the café offers only limited spaces for cars. That said, the excellent taste and inviting atmosphere more than make up for this inconvenience. Whether you're a casual drinker or a connoisseur, KAME KAFE is worth the visit for its standout beverages and relaxing vibe.

user_reviews.Description:
The first thing we noticed was the lack of attentiveness from the staff, something we’ve never experienced before in Thailand. We had already reached out to the place on Agoda, but they never got back to us. Upon arrival around 7pm, we spent 10 minutes walking around the lobby area calling for someone to help us check in. Ultimately a guest staying there helped us get one of the staff members, a male guard, who was drinking and having a party with his buddy at a staff area. They laughed with each other every time we asked a question. It felt very unprofessional and made for a poor check-in experience. We tried to give them the benefit of the doubt, but their attitude continued.

Another odd thing is that you have to pay 400 THB to take a photo with the caged animals on the property.

As for the location, it’s quite remote. You’ll need to pay around 500 THB for a Grab ride to get anywhere, and the resort doesn’t offer scooter rentals. Very odd place, although the rooms are nice, there is a weird vibe around the resort, especially if you’re solo. I would suggest to avoid this place and find a better one.

Staying here for a couple of days still, let’s see if there will be any improvements soon.

title: Beanbag coffee
address: 89 Beanbag coffee, 9, Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
This café is located right by the main road, with a large parking lot that can fit around 15-20 cars, which is super convenient.

The café space is just the right size: there’s a coffee bar where you can order drinks and desserts, plus several private glass rooms indoors. Even though it’s right next to the main road, the atmosphere is surprisingly quiet.

Note that they only serve coffee and desserts here—no main meals—but both the coffee and sweet treats are delicious.

The outdoor area is lovely too, with lawns and large trees that provide plenty of shade, making it a great spot to relax.

We actually use meeting room services quite often, and at first, we planned to make this cafe our main place for client meetings and regular visits. But after today’s experience, we now have to reconsider whether we would like to come back again.

title: Farm Story House
address: 126 Soi Mu Ban Wang Tan Villa, Pa Daet Sub-district, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50100

complete_address.street: 126 Soi Mu Ban Wang Tan Villa

user_reviews.Description:
I stopped by around noon, during peak sun, and ended up having the place to myself which made the whole experience even better.

☕ Drinks: I had a medium roast and one of their signature drinks (Chaos). Both were excellent.

🎧 Atmosphere: This is the kind of space a lot of coffee shops try to create: curated, artsy, “work-friendly”. Most miss the mark, but this one actually pulls it off without feeling forced. The music was perfect, and the books and artwork felt natural rather than staged. The whole place has a genuinely relaxed, authentic vibe.

💻 Work-Friendly: An ideal spot if you’re working remotely or just want to ease into your morning.

🤝 Service & Expertise: The owner took the time to walk me through coffee and roasting and gave me tips to improve how I use my moka pot at home. He’s incredibly knowledgeable and there’s an almost scientific approach behind everything they do.

🧪 For Coffee Lovers: If you’re into coffee or even just curious about more experimental drinks, this is top tier. Nothing about it felt overdone. just thoughtful, real, and easy to enjoy.

title: Take a Walk
address: 98 Baan Pongsamaki, Pa Miang, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
"Take a walk" is one of those amazing places where you say who on earth put this together and was it worth it.

It's certainly worth it for visitors though it's not a widely known attraction.  You find it by heading out of Chiang Mai to the Doi Saket area on route 118, and then turn right onto route 3005, carrying on for about 2 kilometres until you see a small road sign saying "Take a walk coffee."

The walk to the attraction is approximately 150 metres over a couple of swaying bridges and over very uneven ground. Not really dangerous but do take care doing this journey, particularly if you have children.

Most children would love it here provided you took their devices off them.  Many adults would find it a very scenic, quiet place to have a coffee.

Apart from the excellent scenery around nature and a river, there is a rustic adventure playground which is quite amazing to see and children would surely love it.

Out of the way, but certainly worth the visit if you're in that area.

user_reviews.Description:
Good food, but not as cheap as people often say.

I ordered the smoked salmon Eggs Benedict, and I have to say the taste is good. The eggs were nicely cooked, and the hollandaise sauce was tasty and well balanced, not too heavy. Overall, it’s a satisfying brunch dish.

That said, I don’t really agree with the idea that this café is “cheap.” Most dishes come with white bread toast by default, and if you want to change it to sourdough, you need to add 30 baht. Once you factor that in, the final price becomes very similar to other cafés in Chiang Mai that offer the same kind of Eggs Benedict and brunch menu.

So yes, the food is good and enjoyable, but price-wise it’s quite standard, not significantly cheaper than other comparable cafés.

A decent option for brunch, just don’t expect it to be much more affordable than others offering similar dishes.

user_reviews.Description:
Siting in this courtyard, enjoying the food…
For a moment I forgot where I am and I was transported in to a french fairytale.
Dining here is an experience. I feel honored.
There are some other “western” cafés in Chang Mai that feel more like a money extraction operation but here I feel truly welcome and the staff’s intention is really to deliver the most  excellence to the highest quality standards possible. I have personally talked to the owners and I get the sense that they really love what they do and have a true passion for food.
You can be sure that anything you try will be beautifully presented, quality sourced ingredients, and a courteous service with a smile. The setting is so beautiful and well designed. It is peaceful and pleasant. It is a bit pricey, but the value you get is absolutely justified.

I’m so happy to have found this place and will be coming back again and again.

Thank You very much Petite Gardin! Bravo!

user_reviews.Description:
We came to check out the place because of the good reviews about it but a bit disappointing with the taste of the bubble tea. We feel that it’s about an average bubble tea.

We tried 2 different tea—Taiwanese Bubble Tea and Midnight Cacao Brown Sugar Bubble tea. The Taiwanese Bubble Tea was just average like we mentioned earlier although the bubble are quite nice, soft but with good texture. The other one, Midnight Cacao Brown Sugar Bubble Tea was overpowering with the cacao flavor competing with quite sweet brown sugar bubbles and it didn’t taste like anything special about the cacao flavor actually.

Price wise, it’s quite expensive, except for the plain Taiwanese Bubble Tea. We have tried different bubble tea from other places and there are places that make better bubble tea with reasonable price than this.

What we like about this place is it has a potential to make you feel cozy with its minimal Japanese style of decoration. But, we only give actually 2.5 stars for this place because the place feels cluttered with many employees working behind the counter and yet, work gets done quite slowly. From our experiences traveling and visiting many places, small place like this would probably need not more than 2 people working in one shift. They had 5 people working behind a small counter at the time we were visiting the place and it makes the place feel so cramped and loud inside and like we said... it takes time to get your order. So, it wasn’t a pleasant place to sit and relax. The place lacks friendly vibes actually.

So, the best part about this place is its plain bubbles.

title: Round n Round
address: Round n Round 8/3, Tha Sala Sub-district, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50000

user_reviews.Description:
When I say 10/10 I mean it!! The food, the service, the atmosphere.

The owner of the restaurant is so kind and makes sure that everyone who enters her shop feels welcomed and appreciated.

Nice open space with lots of natural light and solid WiFi, good for getting a solid meal and doing some work on your laptop.

The food itself is on another level. The jambon-beurre sandwich with apricot jam/butter/ham and the kimchi bacon cheese sandwich had flavors that I didn’t even know was possible! lol a very different experience.

The desserts deserve their own applause too. We tried their brand new lemon curd cream cheese brioche donut. My GOD if you go here for anything please get this donut. You will not regret it. Also the tiramisu cake was FIRE.

If there’s one place to visit while in Chiang Mai, this is it. 100/10!!!

title: MINTNIMAL
address: 65 Prapokklao Road Old City Tambon Phra Sing, เมือง Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
So we actually went to Chiang Mai. I found this ice cream shop highly recommended all over 点评 and Google.

It is super popular mainly because of its old-school vintage ambience. The whole space is decorated with retro furniture, matched with a soft mint Tiffany tone, bringing out a warm cottage vibe, which easily draws people in.

They specialised uniquely in mint flavoured ice cream. The weather in Chiang Mai was unbearably hot, so having something cold and minty was exactly what I needed. Since I personally love mint, we decided to drop by.

It was scorching hot outside, yet the moment you step inside, the cold air conditioning hits you instantly, making the temperature contrast incredibly comforting.

Since my husband doesn’t eat ice cream, I ended up ordering three flavours all by myself. I thought I travelled all the way here, there was no way I would leave without trying them.

The mint taste was mild and refreshing, without any weird toothpaste aftertaste. I also had the Raspberry Mango flavour, which tasted just like a light fruity sorbet. It was tangy, fresh and absolutely lovely.

The texture was genuinely well-balanced. Each ice cream scoop is just the right portion, not overly big. It is neither too creamy nor overly icy.

Of course, I couldn’t finish all three scoops, only about one and a half. But for me, getting to taste everything is always the priority.

This place is perfect as a little rest pit stop, ideal for popping in to enjoy a nice cup of ice cream to cool down while wandering around Chiang Mai.

title: Mountain Coffee by Noi
address: 6 Ratvithi 2 Alley Old City Tambon Si Phum, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
A Flavor Journey in Every Cup: Chiang Dao Coffee with the Most Unique Finish

This Old City gem offers a complete artisan experience that starts with your palate and ends with a story. Beyond their incredible hand-roasted, organic Chiang Dao Arabica coffee and exceptional homemade breads, they serve a cup with a truly unique taste profile.

Coffee Experience: Their must-try Iced Americano showcases beans roasted right on-site. But here’s what sets it apart: the taste journey. It begins with a surprisingly sweet, bright palette—notes of citrus and honey—that then transforms into a distinct, intentional, warming "burn" at the finish. It’s not bitter; it’s a complex, almost smoky depth that lingers beautifully. This unique progression from sweet to roasted warmth is unforgettable.

Perfect Pairings: The homemade Mum's Banana Bread (walnuts, whole wheat, honey) complements the coffee's sweetness, while their Flourless Seed & Nut Bread (no yeast/dairy) stands up to its robust finish.

More than a café—it's a destination for those who appreciate craftsmanship in both coffee and food. A must-visit for a complete, sophisticated experience in the Old City.

**A Hidden Gem for Coffee Lovers**

Tucked away in the heart of Chiang Mai old town, this coffee shop is an absolute delight for anyone who appreciates great coffee and a cozy ambiance. From the moment you step inside, you're welcomed by the rich aroma of freshly brewed coffee and a warm, inviting atmosphere.

The menu boasts a variety of high-quality coffees, from perfectly crafted espresso shots to creamy, indulgent lattes. I opted for their signature latte, and it was *perfection*—smooth, velvety, and brewed to bring out the nuanced flavors of their beans. For those who prefer something beyond coffee, their selection of homemade healthy breads and granola is equally impressive.

The owner/ barista is not only skilled but also incredibly friendly, taking the time to explain options and make personalized recommendations.

If you’re a coffee aficionado or just someone looking for a great spot to unwind, this place is a must-visit. I can’t wait to come back for more.

**Rating: 5/5**

Review of Coffee or Me

Coffee or Me is a charming café nestled within a hotel, which I happened upon by chance while driving through the area. It’s an ideal spot for those seeking a quiet, nature-filled retreat to work or unwind, offering a refreshing contrast to the bustling cafés in downtown Chiang Mai. With its lush greenery and serene atmosphere, the setting is undeniably inviting.

However, when it comes to the coffee, I found it somewhat underwhelming—perhaps because the café prioritizes ambiance over the quality of its brews. Additionally, the service felt a bit distant, which slightly detracted from the overall experience. A more attentive approach to customer service could enhance both the atmosphere and the coffee itself, making this hidden gem even more enjoyable.

user_reviews.Description:
This was my third visit to Sunday Baker, and I’ve always liked the atmosphere. The café has a lovely, elegant vibe, and it feels even more spacious than when I first visited. This time, I brought my partner for breakfast. We’re both big bagel lovers, so we were excited to give theirs a try. Unfortunately, we found them pretty average. The bagels were a bit too chewy and difficult to cut, and some of the ingredients didn’t quite work for my taste. I did enjoy the detox juice, though I wish the portion had been a little more generous.

The biggest downside for me has always been the parking. The café is located near a tricky intersection, and reversing out can be quite stressful. We spent over 700 THB on breakfast for two, which felt a little steep for what we got. Sunday Baker is still a lovely spot if you enjoy a pretty café with a relaxed atmosphere, but personally, I think three visits have been enough for me.

user_reviews.Description:
Bartcoffee is a small coffee shop located under a tamarind tree in Soi Muang Mueang, Chiang Mai.

The shop has a cozy interior with seating available both inside and at the bar, and it is located close to a barista. When I visited, I had the Espresso Aroma, which was fantastic, with a fruity taste.

As I sipped on the Dirty Coffee, I was immediately struck by the rich, sweet, and creamy flavor. The homemade syrup added a unique sweetness and depth to the drink, while the chilled milk provided a creamy, refreshing texture.

Overall, I highly recommend trying the Dirty Coffee at Bartcoffee. It's a perfect example of the coffee shop's commitment to quality and creativity, and it's sure to satisfy any coffee lover's taste buds.

Parking may be a bit difficult to find as the coffee shop is located in a small alley, but it makes for a peaceful and quiet atmosphere. If you happen to visit on a cool day in Chiang Mai, it's even better.

Facebook : From The Earth To A Cup

The cafe itself seems enticing at first. Nice modern fit out with cool waiters.   When we arrived, it was suspiciously empty : only one other table. We ordered the Khao Soi Fettucini and a Wagyu Fried Rice. We then waited. 20 minutes later, the waiter came back and said they were sold out of the wagyu. It was then I realised they hadn’t started cooking at all. So I changed it to a slow cooked pork curry - knowing that they probably had this prepared since it needs hours slow cooking.

So we waited. And waited. And waited. In the meantime, the staff had gone missing. Some other table had to go inside to find some service staff.

We finally had our meals after 35 minutes of waiting. The slow cooked pork curry had been reheated, but was leaning on the lukewarm side. The fettucini was fusion khao soi fettucini , but ended up less tasty than either dish.

But oh my, the wait! The wait wasn’t worth it for us, but for people who have a lot of time on their hands to waste, it may be worth it for them.

So we waited. And waited. And waited. In the meantime, the staff had gone missing. Some other table had to go inside to find some service staff.

We finally had our meals after 35 minutes of waiting. The slow cooked pork curry had been reheated, but was leaning on the lukewarm side. The fettucini was fusion khao soi fettucini , but ended up less tasty than either dish.

But oh my, the wait! The wait wasn’t worth it for us, but for people who have a lot of time on their hands to waste, it may be worth it for them.

title: Hannah • Hahn
address: 289 Hannah • Hahn, 2, Mae Hia, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50100

user_reviews.Description:
We chose this restaurant to celebrate my mother-in-law's birthday, hoping for a memorable meal. Unfortunately, the food was a disappointment and affected what should have been a happy occasion.

The Massaman Chicken did not look or taste like an authentic Thai Massaman curry. It lacked the rich, creamy, aromatic, and slightly sweet flavor expected from this dish. The crushed peanuts were simply sprinkled on top rather than being cooked together with the curry, which made it feel more like a shortcut preparation.

The Sab Hang was extremely sour, and the excessive sourness completely overpowered the other flavors. The chicken steak was also disappointing. The chicken breast was dry and overcooked, while the red sauce was thin and watery, tasting more like red wine than a proper steak sauce. The only decent part of this dish was the side dishes.

The fish with mango salad was another letdown. The fish itself was bland, while the mango sauce was too salty. The fish should have been crispy, but it appeared to have been sitting in the sauce for too long, making it soggy instead of crisp.

The spaghetti was very bland and lacked seasoning, as if it was missing salt and proper flavor. The deep-fried items were just average with nothing memorable. The fried rice was ordinary but still one of the better dishes compared to the others.

For dessert, we ordered the Orange Cake and London Chocolate Caramel Cake. The Orange Cake was just a normal sponge cake with an orange layer, nothing special. The London Chocolate Caramel Cake was disappointing as there was no noticeable caramel flavor, and the use of salted buttercream instead of fresh cream made the cake taste salty and bitter when combined with the chocolate.

The only positive items were the roti served with the Massaman curry and the side dishes from the chicken steak.

According to the staff, the restaurant has two chefs—one foreign chef and one local chef. I was told that our dishes were prepared by the local chef. Unfortunately, based on this experience, I hope the restaurant can ensure consistent quality regardless of which chef is cooking.

I sincerely hope the owner takes the time to personally taste the dishes served to customers. Regularly checking the food quality is important to ensure it meets the restaurant's own standards. I hope this feedback is taken constructively to improve the dining experience for future customers.

Recommended.

user_reviews.Description:
True masters of espresso. This is one of those rare places where every step of the process is done with precision and respect for the craft. You can choose between a medium roast Thai–Laos blend or a dark roast Thai blend — both roasted and extracted perfectly.

Each bean type has its own dedicated grinder, calibrated to deliver exactly 15 grams of coffee. After dosing, the barista uses WDT needles to evenly distribute the grounds, followed by a leveler and tamper for perfect consistency. The extraction is spot-on: 30 ml in precisely 30 seconds.

The result? A flawless almond-colored crema, a cup that’s neither overheated nor under-extracted — just beautifully balanced and full of character. Every espresso is served with a small glass of water (I’d personally suggest a slightly smaller one, since it’s meant just to cleanse the palate — but that’s a minor, personal note).

For this level of attention to detail and repeatable perfection, you could easily compete with some of the best espresso bars in Italy or Portugal.

And honestly — if I had to choose anyone’s espresso (apart from my own 😉) — I’d choose yours!
Congratulations, Rich Coffee House — truly exceptional work.

user_reviews.Description:
Thingamajiggy and Rab A Bit have officially earned a spot on my all-time favorites list. 🤍

Thingamajiggy is the kind of place where simply being there brings a sense of calm. Sipping coffee while gazing across the rice fields on a beautiful day feels like pure bliss. The architecture blends seamlessly with the mountains, the paddies, and the surrounding community. A beautiful creation by Yarng Na Studio, simple, serene, and effortlessly elegant. It’s the kind of place that makes me want to move to Mae Rim.

You can feel the heart behind it. It doesn’t seem like a place that was created with a business-first mindset, yet somehow that authenticity has become its greatest strength. And that’s exactly what makes it so special.

As for Rab A Bit, every dish feels like a warm home-cooked meal, and every bite is satisfying until the very last. Their stir-fried noodles with shrimp and fresh chili are simply outstanding. I love Rab A Bit, I really do!

A place worth returning to again and again, and I genuinely believe anyone who visits will feel the same. 🩵

I visited Why Coffee and Bar for the first time by accident — and it turned out to be a great discovery.

After speaking with the barista, I learned that the owner started this coffee journey four years ago with a small Rocket espresso machine. Today, they’ve grown into a proper space with their own roaster, which is truly impressive.

Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates well-crafted specialty coffee in Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Description:
Weave Artisan Society has become one of my favorite places in Chiang Mai. It is this big, open warehouse style cafe that feels trendy yet still a bit off the beaten path for most digital nomads, so you get a really nice mix of locals and entrepreneurs. It is usually not overly busy, the vibe is relaxed, and the coffee and food are good.

It is also a great and somewhat unexpected place to invite clients or partners for meetings, because the space feels professional without being stiff. Me and some friends have also hosted events there recently and the venue has been very accommodating and easy to work with.

They recently opened the new coworking space upstairs, which I am renting on a monthly basis, and I absolutely love it. The team is very accommodating, the layout never feels overcrowded, and there is a lot of flexibility for how you want to work or meet people. They keep making thoughtful improvements, and I am genuinely looking forward to seeing how the space continues to grow.

user_reviews.Description:
A café I keep coming back to. It’s one of my favorite pet-friendly places around here.

What I really love is the greenery. The whole area is full of big trees and open space, which makes the atmosphere very relaxing and easy on the eyes. The place is quite spacious too, so even when there are many people it still feels comfortable and not crowded.

It works well for many types of visitors. Families with kids can enjoy the playground, and if you come with pets there’s a big lawn where they can walk around freely. If you come with your partner or friends, there are also plenty of seating spots to choose from.

Another fun thing is that you can feed the turtles. The breeze flows through the area nicely so it doesn’t feel too hot, even during the day.

They serve food, cakes, and drinks, and there are also toys and alcohol available. Parking is easy because there’s plenty of space.

Always a nice place to relax and spend time. I’ve already been here several times and will definitely come back again.

user_reviews.Description:
A little gem tucked inside Chiang Mai's Old City. This place strikes the perfect balance between cozy and functional — you can grab a seat indoors with the AC cranking or settle in outside if you want to soak up the atmosphere. Either way, the vibe is warm and relaxed without feeling too try-hard.

The coffee menu has solid variety, so whether you're a black coffee purist or want something a little more creative, you'll find something that works. I went with the bagel breakfast sandwich and it did not disappoint.

The staff were genuinely friendly and made the whole experience feel welcoming rather than transactional, which goes a long way.

If you're wandering the moat area and need a proper sit-down spot to recharge, this is the move. Already planning to come back on my next visit.

user_reviews.Description:
We stumbled across this little cafe on our first day, which was very close to our hotel (Shangri-la). It's run by a lovely family (mum cooks, father makes the drinks, daughter makes the waffles). Service can be slow if crowded, as there's only one cook. But the food more than makes up for it.

Everything we tried was really delicious! But the star of the show is the mango stick rice. One of the best we've ever tried!

We ended up eating here 3 times during our short stay in Chiang Mai.

The owner of the cafe (R) was really friendly and lovely to chat with. His command of the English language is pretty good so it was fun chatting with him.

If you're looking for authentic Thai food, and really amazing mango stick rice, head to Rywin cafe! High recommended!

Bonus: They open before 9am, so you can head there for breakfast. Their full menu is available for breakfast as well.

user_reviews.Description:
You can live abroad for years, eat like a local, learn the rhythms, and swear you don’t miss a thing.

Then one random morning your brain whispers, not in Thai: tuna sandwich.

I’ve had plenty over the last couple of years, chasing that simple, salty, familiar bite like it’s a postcard from another life. And without a doubt, Poon Coffee & Restaurant (พูนคอฟฟี่) makes the best tuna sandwich in all of Chiang Mai.

It starts with the bread. Toasted just right, that sweet spot between sturdy and tender. Light butter. The kind of toast that makes a quiet crunch and then gets out of the way.

Then the tuna. Not a polite little smear. A real amount. Seasoned well, stacked between three slices of bread like someone decided you deserved a double-decker moment.

On the side: crisp lettuce, tomatoes, onions, plus a slice of watermelon and dragonfruit, like a small edible reminder that you’re not back home at all, and that’s kind of the point.

I washed it down with an Americano, the way I always do. Ice water alongside. A small cookie, because Thailand is generous like that.

“Heaven” is a big word, but breakfast like this earns it. If you’re in Chiang Mai and you get that sudden craving for something that tastes like memory, go see the good people at Poon Coffee & Restaurant. They’ll take care of you.

P.S. they have lots of Thai and Western food too!

user_reviews.Description:
Victor French Bakery is a charming little hidden gem, tucked away at the end of a narrow alley between other buildings, so it can be a bit difficult to spot at first. But it is absolutely worth the visit.

They serve an impressive selection of delicious pastries and baked goods, along with great coffee and a variety of both hot and cold drinks. There is a lovely outdoor seating area, but if you prefer air conditioning, there is also plenty of comfortable seating inside.

The bakery is very family friendly as well, with a small corner for children that includes a TV and some toys, so feel free to bring the kids along.

What really makes this place special is the staff, always smiling, welcoming, helpful, and skilled at what they do. They make you feel right at home from the moment you walk in.

title: de forest
address: Kotchasarn Rd, Chang Khlan Sub-district, Muang Chiang Mai 50100

user_reviews.Description:
I left this little brunch spot with a smile. The food wasn’t absolutely perfect, and there were a few things that could be improved, but the affordable prices, beautiful setting and especially the owner’s kindness made it a memorable experience. I’m happy to give it five stars for the overall experience.

I ordered French toast and a milkshake. I don’t remember the exact bill, but I believe the total was under 300 THB, which felt very reasonable for such a substantial, colourful brunch. The plate came with French toast, mango and an assortment of other fruits, along with little containers of sauce. The milkshake arrived in a lovely purple shade, decorated with flowers. It was a very cheerful-looking meal, against the patterned tablecloth.

I do want to be fair about the presentation. When the food first arrived, it didn’t look quite as polished as the menu photograph. The mangoes were smaller than I had imagined, and the way some of the fruit had been cut and arranged wasn’t particularly photogenic at first. I actually spent a little time adjusting the arrangement before taking my own pictures. Once I had done that, however, I was delighted with the photos! The colourful fruit, bright flowers and purple drink made such a pretty combination. If you’re visiting mainly for pictures, just be aware that the plate may not look exactly like the promotional image when it first reaches your table.

Taste-wise, the French toast was enjoyable enough, though not something I would describe as extraordinary. There was plenty of fruit flavour alongside the toast, but the combination didn’t completely win me over. It was pleasant rather than unforgettable. The milkshake, on the other hand, was genuinely delicious. I enjoyed it much more than the toast, and it was probably my favourite part of the order. It looked beautiful and tasted great too,

The restaurant has an outdoor setting, which gives it a relaxed, open-air feeling. I liked the atmosphere, but there were flies around the food. I understand that this can be difficult to prevent in an outdoor restaurant, and I don’t want to judge the place too harshly for something that is partly a consequence of its setting. Still, it did make the meal a little less comfortable, and guests who are particularly bothered by insects may want to keep that in mind.

The service was a mixture of experiences. The owner was genuinely lovely, friendly and welcoming, and that warmth made a real difference to my visit. I did feel a little overlooked by a younger male staff member at times. I can’t know whether it was intentional, but I would have appreciated a little more attentiveness. Thankfully, my interactions with the owner were much more positive and left the strongest impression.

What made the visit especially sweet was that the owner gave me a small bag as a gift. I hadn’t expected anything like that, and I was touched by the gesture. It was a thoughtful surprise. Small acts of kindness can change how you remember a place, and this one certainly did for me.

I also think the pricing deserves real credit. Brunch dishes that look this colourful and elaborate can easily feel overpriced, but here I felt I was getting a lot for my money. Even though the toast wasn’t my favourite and the presentation needed a little adjustment, I never felt disappointed about what I had spent. The milkshake was delicious, the setting was charming,

My five stars are for the whole experience rather than a claim that every detail was flawless. I hope the team can improve the consistency of the food presentation, be a little more attentive to every guest, and do what they can about flies near the tables. But I also hope they keep the friendly, personal atmosphere that makes this place special. Thank you to the owner for the warm welcome and the thoughtful little gift. I left happy and will remember this brunch fondly.

user_reviews.Description:
On the pond!!! Bella Goose is one of those rare places that quietly becomes part of your routine—and then your memory.

This location is especially beautiful. Tucked away and peaceful, it feels like a quiet oasis where time slows down just enough. Same incredible coffee as their other spots, made with the same care and intention. Coffee here isn’t just served—it’s respected.

I ordered my go-to, the piccolo, and it was flawless as always—silk-smooth, perfectly textured, with a bold, confident espresso that lingers. Easily among the best espresso I’ve had in Thailand. Knowing they roast their own beans and source through real relationships with local farmers makes every cup feel even more thoughtful. And whoever’s behind the bar—absolute talent. Getting latte art right once is hard; getting a piccolo to arrive looking like a tiny painting every time is real craft.

I also had the honey lemon soda, which was refreshing and perfect for cooling down—just as dialed in as their coffee.

But what truly makes Bella Goose special, at any location, is the people. The warmest, kindest staff I encountered in Thailand—no question. They go beyond service, You don’t just feel welcomed, you feel at home. That kind of consistency comes from great leadership and a team that genuinely loves what they do.

Whether you’re meeting friends, getting work done, or just sitting by the pond with a great drink, Bella Goose is a place to linger. I couldn’t recommend it more.

If you’re ever in Mae Rim, don’t just come here for the coffee — come for the whole experience: nature, good vibes, and giving back. 🌱✨

user_reviews.Description:
An absolute gem in Chiang Mai! 🤎

I spent a wonderful, peaceful moment here – exactly the kind of gentle day I needed. I stayed for over two hours, reading and journaling in this incredibly soothing atmosphere.

As a pastry chef from France, I can say their Tiramisu was truly excellent. The quality is outstanding: refined, perfectly balanced, not too sweet, with a rich cocoa flavor. A real treat! I also had a sparkling Honey & Lemon Matcha, which was refreshing and perfectly executed.

The cafe is a true haven of serenity. It’s amazing how calm this little alley is, even though it's right near a main street and a car dealership. I loved taking photos for my memories; every corner is so photogenic.

The staff is lovely, smiling, and very well-organized. I really enjoyed watching them work in their kitchen (the second room has a charming 'country house' vibe). It almost made me want to jump in and start baking with them!

I recommend this place 1000%, whether for the quality of the desserts or the warm welcome. I’ll definitely be back to try the Carrot Cake. Thank you for a perfect afternoon! ✨

I've been coming here for a month now and I felt the need to update my review...

We should normalize going back to the places that make us feel good, over and over again.
During my month in Chiang Mai, Zmoy Cafe became my sanctuary. It was the place I returned to several times a week whenever I needed comfort, silence, or a moment of peace.

Beyond the technical excellence—because everything here is perfectly mastered, from the subtle sugar balance to the coffee quality that easily rivals the best shops in France—it’s the soul of the place that stays with you. It is a little slice of paradise tucked away in the Old City where you immediately feel at home.

It has become my personal 'Proust’s Madeleine' in Thailand. I love the reassuring consistency: the service is always gentle and kind, and the homemade pastries always taste just as delicious, time after time. They don't try to do everything; they focus on what they do best, and you can feel the heart they put into it—from their social media to the way they treat every customer.

If there is one thing I will truly miss about Chiang Mai, it’s the feeling of warmth I got every time I walked through those doors. It’s not a goodbye, just a 'see you later.' I highly recommend anyone to stop here, step away from the dust and noise, and just enjoy the moment.

user_reviews.Description:
I visited Versailles de Flore one morning with a friend for breakfast and to take photos. My main expectation was based on the Renaissance-style decoration inspired by the Palace of Versailles in France, so I initially imagined a more refined, luxury like experience.

In reality, it is not a luxury place, but rather a lovely and peaceful café with beautiful decor. The setting is very well done and makes you feel like you are walking through a small European museum. It’s a calm place and perfect for taking photos.

The breakfast was good. I ordered fried eggs served in a pan, accompanied by fish sausage, minced pork, toasted bread with butter and a touch of garlic, plus a small salad with lettuce and cherry tomatoes. I also had a cappuccino, which was nicely prepared.

There is no table service; you need to order and pay at the counter first, and then the staff brings your food. When we visited around 10 a.m., there was only one waiter and the cook, so the service felt simple and casual.

Prices are not high or exaggerated at all, they are very reasonable and comparable to other cafés in Chiang Mai, even those with much simpler designs. Coffee starts around 65–70 THB, which I found fair considering the atmosphere.
Overall, my experience was good, even though it was different from what I originally expected. I would recommend this place if you are looking for a beautiful, quiet, and photogenic café, as long as you don’t expect a luxury dining experience

user_reviews.Description:
A Beautiful, Pet-Friendly Café in Chiang Mai With Amazing Matcha & Fresh Pastries

Dorle Coffee Shop in Chiang Mai is truly one of the most charming and peaceful cafés in the city. If you’re searching for a relaxing spot with great drinks, delicious pastries, and a pet-friendly environment, this place is a must-visit.

One of the highlights is their pure matcha (clear matcha) — it’s absolutely spot on. Smooth, refreshing, and perfectly balanced, it’s one of the best matcha drinks you can find in Chiang Mai. They also offer a delightful selection of freshly baked pastries, all of which are incredibly yummy. Whether you love buttery croissants or other treats, everything tastes freshly made. They even have sourdough, which is a big plus for bread lovers.

Dorle is also wonderfully pet friendly. Dogs are welcome inside the air-conditioned area as long as they don’t disturb other customers, making it an ideal café for hot Chiang Mai days. Their outdoor garden is another highlight—lush, beautifully manicured, and truly zen, perfect for relaxing with your drink or spending quiet time with your furry friend.

The staff are lovely, polite, and genuinely friendly, adding to the overall warm and welcoming atmosphere.

If you’re looking for a pet-friendly café in Chiang Mai, a spot with excellent matcha, or a garden coffee shop with fresh pastries and sourdough, Dorle Coffee Shop is absolutely worth supporting and visiting. Highly recommended!

title: Baan Chiangroong
address: V4CG+H87 Baan Chiangroong, Luang Nuea, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
Baan Chiangroong Café is such a hidden gem, tucked right in front of a charming hotel near my sister’s house. She took me there for the first time, and I instantly fell in love with the atmosphere.

The café has a warm, homey feel, beautifully decorated with vintage wooden furniture that gives it a cozy, nostalgic charm. It truly feels like you’re enjoying coffee in someone’s lovely old home rather than a commercial café. Surrounded by lush greenery and natural light, it’s the kind of place that invites you to slow down and relax.

The menu is simple yet delightful. They serve a great selection of coffee, tea, and other drinks, all at very reasonable prices. The cakes are a must-try—soft, fresh, and only 40 baht per slice, which is such great value. They also offer a variety of breakfast options, perfect for both locals and hotel guests looking for a peaceful morning meal.

The café has free Wi-Fi, making it an ideal spot to sit and work or read while sipping your drink. Parking is convenient as well, with several spaces available inside the property, and you can also park along the street in front of the hotel if needed.

Overall, Baan Chiangroong Café is a lovely little spot that combines comfort, good food, and genuine local charm. Whether you’re looking for a quiet place to start your morning or a cozy café to spend a lazy afternoon, this one is definitely worth visiting.

Dr. Niwech

title: Palore Coffee & Tea House
address: 88, Palore Coffee & Tea House, Thep Sadet, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
Palore Coffee & Tea House – A Hidden Gem in the Hills of Doi Saket
Tucked away in the misty hills of Thep Sadet, Doi Saket, Palore Coffee & Tea House is easily one of the most memorable café stops in the Chiang Mai countryside. The drive out is part of the charm — winding mountain roads through the coffee-growing village of Ban Pang Hai lead you somewhere that feels worlds away from the city, and the payoff is absolutely worth it.
The first thing that strikes you is the setting. The café is built across several levels, with a striking multi-story suspension bridge stretching up toward a treehouse-style viewing platform. Walking to the top rewards you with sweeping views over the surrounding hills and village, especially beautiful in the early morning when fog rolls through the valley. It's the kind of spot that makes you want to put your phone away and just take it all in — though of course, it's also a fantastic photo opportunity if you're into that.
As for the coffee itself, it's genuinely excellent. Palore grows and roasts its own beans locally, and you can taste the difference. The espresso has a bright, slightly fruity edge to it, and the drip coffee is smooth and full of character. If you're a tea person, they haven't been left behind either — Palore has its own house tea brand, and the hot cappuccino and iced Americano both come highly recommended by regulars. Even the food menu, which mixes Thai dishes with simple Western options, holds its own alongside the drinks.
One of the best surprises is the pricing. Given the setting and the quality of what's on offer, it's remarkably affordable — this isn't a place that charges a premium just because the view is Instagram-worthy. You can easily spend a whole afternoon here without breaking the bank.
The atmosphere throughout is relaxed and unhurried. Seating is spread across the different levels of the building, with a small artificial waterfall adding to the calm, natural feel. There are plenty of quiet corners if you want to sit and read or work, and equally plenty of scenic spots if you're there with friends or family looking for a good time and good photos. It has the kind of unpretentious charm that places like Mae Kampong are known for, without the crowds.
Before you leave, it's worth stopping by the little shop on site — they sell their own roasted coffee beans, dried tea, and locally produced macadamia nut oil, all nicely packaged and perfect for taking home or gifting.
All in all, Palore Coffee & Tea House delivers on every front: genuinely good coffee, a gorgeous natural setting, a fun bit of adventure with the suspension bridge, and prices that won't leave you wincing at the bill. If you're exploring the Doi Saket area or doing a café-hopping day trip through the hills east of Chiang Mai, this one deserves a spot at the top of your list. Highly recommended.

Mai Bakery in Garden is such a charming and cozy spot; it instantly gives you that warm, farmhouse feeling the moment you step inside. The interior design feels just like a countryside home in Texas, with rustic wooden furniture, soft colors, and lovely vintage decorations that make you feel right at home. The whole place is surrounded by greenery, making it a peaceful retreat for anyone who loves nature and good food.

The café offers a wide selection of dishes, freshly baked cakes, and excellent coffee. Whether you’re in the mood for a hearty breakfast, a light brunch, or just a slice of cake with a cup of latte, Mai Bakery in Garden has something for everyone. Everything is beautifully presented and tastes just as good as it looks.

One of the best parts about this place is that it’s connected to a hotel; making it incredibly convenient for hotel guests. Imagine waking up in the morning and walking just a few steps to enjoy your breakfast in a lovely garden atmosphere, surrounded by flowers, trees, and fresh air. It’s the perfect way to start the day.

Mai Bakery in Garden is not just a café, it’s a relaxing experience. Whether you come for the food, the cozy ambiance, or just to unwind with a book and a cup of coffee, you’ll leave feeling refreshed and happy. It’s truly one of those hidden gems you’ll want to return to again and again.

Dr. Niwech

title: Mix Kaffee
address: 29 Arak Rd Old City Tambon Si Phum, เมือง Chiang Mai 50000

user_reviews.Description:
This place is a must for any coffee lovers out there. I'd recommend the full course experience for 1500 Bht as each coffee comes paired with an amazing desert to compliment the coffee. You start with water that is infused with smoke from a Cherry Blossom tree to clean the palette and then the experience starts. I was told by the owner that the coffee and dessert pairings change every few months but as of right now the inspiration is walking through a jungle and he really pulled it off. The first coffee was a dark roast to symbolize walking in the jungle with darker notes and was my favorite of the 3 and came with an amazing pastry that tasted of earl grey and had a nice coconut cream to dip it in. The second was symbolized a stream and was amazing while being paired with a Almond pastry that you ate first and the flavor lingered while sipping the coffee. Next was a tiramisu that was soaked in the first dark roast coffee and was amazing! The last symbolized the flowers of a jungle and was fermented for one day in a champagne bottle and then fermented in a airsealed bottle for 5 more days and had such an interesting and amazing flavor. You get so much info and the owner is so friendly and will answer all your questions.

If you're reading this a few months later then the menu will most likely have changed and you'll be lucky enough to try something new and interesting. This will always be a stop for me anytime I'm in Chiang Mai.

title: Rich Mellow
address: Rich Mellow 24/6-24/7 Nimmanahaeminda Road Nimmanhaemin Tambon Su Thep, เมือง Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
A heads-up for future visitors: the café announced a new admission policy on its social media account just six days before my visit. Previously, you could reportedly see the wallabies simply by buying a drink for under 100 THB. Now, admission costs 250 THB, including a 100 THB drink credit. More expensive drinks cost extra, and feeding the animals is another 50 THB. Older reviews may therefore reflect a very different experience in terms of value for money.

The ordering process was confusing. A staff member told me to go to the back to pay, but didn’t explain that the correct entrance was a small doorway off to the side. I naturally entered the much larger, more obvious entrance, which led to an adjoining cannabis shop. The smell was so overwhelmingly strong that it made me nauseous. I rang the bell twice, but nobody came to help.

The staff weren’t particularly welcoming and sometimes sounded abrupt, although they weren’t rude and did patiently answer my questions. My drink was actually quite good.

The three albino wallabies, as confirmed by the staff, were absolutely adorable! Two were in the visitor area, while the third was in a separate area at the back. Most of the time, the animals were sleeping, and there was little interaction until I bought the additional 50 THB food portion. I completely respect their need to rest, but for a one-hour visit at this price, I found the experience rather underwhelming.

I also wondered about the enclosure’s two large glass walls and whether adequate UV protection and shaded spaces were provided for these albino animals, especially under Chiang Mai’s strong sunlight. I couldn’t verify the conditions, but I hope their particular needs are being carefully considered.

Overall, the animals were lovely and the drink was good, but the new pricing, confusing layout, strong cannabis smell nearby, and limited interaction made the visit feel overpriced to me.

user_reviews.Description:
I spent a total of 7 days in Chiang Mai with my girlfriend—4 of them at this lovely café (only because it was unfortunately closed on Sunday). Every time, I ordered a flat white, both with and without oat milk, and each one was absolutely delicious.

The owner is incredibly friendly and truly knows his craft inside and out. He creates the best latte art I’ve ever seen. The café itself doesn’t serve food, so we usually grabbed pastries from London.cnx nearby and enjoyed them here with our coffee, since the two places are very close to each other.

The café is small but beautiful, with a relaxed and cool atmosphere, plus a nice view of the street and the park. I can wholeheartedly recommend this place to everyone!

user_reviews.Description:
Wynn & Tim Cafe is a place I wholeheartedly recommend to anyone who loves cafés. I tried their Matcha Longan drink, and let me tell you—it’s absolutely amazing! The combination of rich, high-quality matcha with the natural sweetness of longan is genius. The flavors are perfectly balanced—bold yet refreshing, with just the right hint of sweetness. It’s the kind of drink that stays on your mind long after you’ve finished it. Honestly, I’m already craving it again! You can truly feel the thought and care that went into creating this menu.

But what truly makes this café special is the owner. They are incredibly kind and welcoming, making you feel more like a guest than just a customer. From the moment I walked in, I felt like I was being warmly welcomed into their space. They even took the time to share the story behind their menu and explained how they carefully select high-quality ingredients. You can see their passion for what they do in every detail—it’s truly inspiring.

The atmosphere at the café is just as impressive. I spent an afternoon here working with a friend, and it was perfect. The peaceful vibe, soft background music, and cozy decor made it so easy to relax and focus. The seating is super comfortable, and the overall ambiance is just so inviting—it’s the kind of place where you could easily spend hours without realizing it.

If you’re looking for a café with exceptional drinks, a welcoming owner, and a peaceful atmosphere, Wynn & Tim Cafe should be at the top of your list. Whatever you do, don’t leave without trying the Matcha Longan—it’s unforgettable. I can’t wait to visit again!

user_reviews.Description: We really enjoyed our outing at Le Petit Zoo so much that we came on Saturday then decided to come again today, just two days later. You can order drinks directly and there is also an option to order food from an extensive food menu (I think the restaurant is next door) but the food looked really good. user_reviews.Description:
If you love animals, please think twice before visiting Le Petit Zoo in Chiang Mai.

I left feeling genuinely sad and depressed after seeing the conditions these poor animals were living in.

The animals were kept in cramped, dirty and extremely hot spaces, with very little to keep them busy. There seemed to be almost nothing for them to do or enjoy.

It was heartbreaking to see animals living in such dull and uncomfortable conditions. Instead of enjoying our visit, I spent the whole time feeling sorry for them and wishing they had a better life.

I cannot understand how anyone could think these conditions are acceptable.

Animals deserve space, clean homes, things to do and a good quality of life. What we saw was the complete opposite.

I would never return, and I strongly urge other animal lovers not to support this place.

If you truly care about animal welfare, please boycott Le Petit Zoo. These animals deserve so much better.

user_reviews.Description: My initial visit was not entirely satisfactory. The music selection, specifically the K-POP dance performance, seemed incongruous with the coffee shop's intended atmosphere, and the volume was somewhat elevated. While I surmise the establishment may be targeting a mid-tier market segment, the overall experience was rather unremarkable. The practice of presenting the bill immediately upon service of coffee and food warrants discussion. Although some establishments adopt this approach to ensure transparency regarding order details, I find it less than optimal for customer engagement. This practice may inadvertently discourage additional purchases due to heightened budget awareness. Furthermore, given that order details were reiterated at the point of payment, the immediate printing of the bill appears to be an unnecessary expenditure of resources and is not environmentally sustainable. On a positive note, the coffee's flavor was exceptional and exceeded my expectations. The staff members were consistently polite and helpful.

user_reviews.Description:
If you're looking for a standout culinary experience in Chiang Mai, The Goodcery is an absolute must-visit. This spot perfectly captures the creative spirit of the city, blending a modern aesthetic with a truly unique menu. What sets them apart is their incredible fusion of Northern Thai and Burmese flavors, which creates a profile you won't find just anywhere.

I personally couldn't get enough of the Jin Top; the flavors were perfectly balanced and left me wanting more. Beyond the food, the ambiance of the place is curated so well, offering a vibe that is both relaxed and inspiring. It feels like the kind of space where quality is prioritized in every detail, from the ingredients to the decor.

The staff are welcoming and clearly passionate about the fusion concept they are presenting. It is a fantastic spot for anyone who appreciates bold spices and thoughtful food presentation. Whether you are a local or just passing through Chiang Mai, this place offers a refreshing break from the more traditional tourist tracks. I found myself lingering just to soak in the atmosphere long after I finished my meal. It’s easily one of my favorite finds in the area, and I will definitely be returning. Don't leave without trying their specialty dishes—your taste buds will thank you!

user_reviews.Description:
A shockingly impressive discovery!   The menu is Burmese known for dishes with salty, sour, bitter, and spicy.  The watermelon w/ the Burmese sauce was spicy bitter salty and sweet a unique and powerful combination making it a must try.   The others we tried was the smoked eggplant dip w/ cucumber again a powerful tasting dish absolutely loved it.  Their meat is meticulously picked out from only one approved vendor to ensure quality and value.  The item is their flank steak and again w/ an exceptional Burmese flavorful sauce.  We ordered another one being it was so amazingly tender and good.
They also try to specialize in offering only organic wines that use very low sulphites sparingly. A+.  We questioned why Michelin hasn’t uncovered this place yet, but being their fairly new it would probably likely explain it.  The sauces make it a gem of a find, really incredible highly recommend!

user_reviews.Description:
I came across this little cafe while i walked earlier the canal.
Its owned by Thai people and you can definitely feel that. There is much more personality behind this little cafe then you think from the first sight.
I am in love with them, because of multiple reasons.
1. their coffee is fabulous, smooth and soooo cheap! One cappuccino is 45baht, 1.20€, and its still so premium!
2. the staff is so friendly, kind and welcoming
3. its good for me, bad for the owner, its so quiet here, i was literally the only person in this cafe.
I hope my review helps to let people know that little gem here in the south of Chiang Mai.
There is also a very nice temple close by.

user_reviews.Description:
One hell of a coffee shop. The space is modest, but the coffee is incredible. No frills, serious bean-lover rodeo over at Three Nakhanik. It’s also pretty cool that they open at 8:33am and close at 3:33pm, and that they project old Cartoon Network cartoons onto the wall. Loved my coffee and the experience.

Update: I finally made it back to CNX and got to revisit THREE. Still love this place and I’m glad they seem to be doing well. I had a split espresso made into a tiny americano and piccolo. I used the Ethiopian bean which was really awesome! It really tasted like toffee. This is one of the best in Chiang Mai, forsure!

Update (Feb 29, 2026): Back once again. Showing a friend around Chiang Mai, and had to come by Three Coffee. Had two lattes, one with Ethiopian beans and one with Panamanian beans. Both were delicious. The shop is still as cool as I recall.

title: CK Cafe
address: 276 ซอย 1 San Phak Wan, Hang Dong District, Chiang Mai 50230

user_reviews.Description:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

CK Café is a true hidden gem in Hang Dong. Nestled in beautiful surroundings with a peaceful koi pond, it's the perfect place to relax and enjoy a great meal.

The food is delicious, the coffee is excellent, and the service is simply outstanding. One thing that really sets this café apart is their willingness to accommodate their guests. If there's something you'd like that's not on the menu, they'll happily prepare it for you, as long as they have the ingredients.

If you don't speak Thai, there's no need to worry. The staff speak fluent English and make you feel welcome from the moment you arrive.

If you're in the Hang Dong area, take a short detour from the main road and discover this wonderful little place. It's well worth the visit, and I'm sure you'll want to come back again.

user_reviews.Description: Everything here was absolutely lovely. The Khao soi is a must have! Many places have great Khao Soi, but the meat on the chicken thigh they used in my wife's dish was so tender it fell right off the bone. I also appreciated that instead of giving me subpar papya salad, they came and explained that it would have been too soft and offered to make a different dish instead AND they brought us fresh mango because they felt bad. I love when a chef has such high standards! The staff was exceptionally nice and so was the ambience. Also, if you are craving a real Thai espresso, they have it here! All around it was a great dining experience.

user_reviews.Description:
I stumbled upon this lovely little coffee shop completely by chance, and it turned out to be one of the most heartwarming experiences I’ve had in Chiang Mai.

The café is run by an elderly couple who were both incredibly kind and welcoming. The coffee was very reasonably priced, with drinks costing around 50 THB or less, and it tasted good too. They could also communicate in simple English, which made ordering easy.

What touched me the most was a small but incredibly thoughtful gesture from the elderly lady. Since the seating area was outdoors, she noticed that I was sitting there enjoying my coffee and kindly brought over a fan, switched it on, and positioned it so that the breeze would blow directly towards me.

I hadn’t asked for it at all. She simply wanted to make sure I was comfortable.

It might seem like a small thing, but that genuine kindness meant so much to me, especially as a traveller visiting somewhere unfamiliar.

I’ve been to much more expensive places where the service felt impersonal, but here, despite the affordable prices, I felt truly welcomed and cared for.

Sometimes the most memorable part of travelling isn’t a famous attraction or an expensive restaurant, but an unexpected moment of kindness from a stranger.

Thank you to this lovely couple for making my day a little brighter. I sincerely hope their little coffee shop continues to do well. They absolutely deserve more customers and recognition.

Highly recommended! ❤️

user_reviews.Description:
We went to this place for lunch and dinner on separate days, and the food did not disappoint. We had different local dishes such as Khao Soi, and everything tasted great. The fried noodles on top of the Khao Soi were very crispy and the curry tasted great (although a little spicy for my tastebuds, but nothing I couldn't manage).

The atmosphere was relaxed and we even sat down to play cards before leaving.

The price for food and drinks were most reasonable - quite inexpensive actually.

This is also the place where I've hands down have had THE best Italian soda in Thailand. My favourite is the one with peach and butterfly pea. It comes with small bits of gelly (which:at first glance seemed a little odd, but I actually really liked it). The syrup used for this Italian soda just tastes better and more like actual fruit than the synthetic syrups used in many other places. We would absolutely come back if we are ever in Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Description:
Rolls.space is such a charming and cozy café that instantly makes you feel at home the moment you walk in.

The space is beautifully designed with plenty of seating options, both comfortable indoor areas with air conditioning and relaxing corners where you can unwind for hours.

It’s a great spot for catching up with friends, working on your laptop, or simply enjoying a quiet afternoon with a good cup of coffee.

The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, with many friendly international visitors, which gives the place a vibrant yet relaxed community feel.

I’ve driven past this café many times since it’s near my friend’s house, but I only recently stopped by, and I’m so glad I did. The coffee is excellent—smooth, rich, and carefully brewed. The food menu is just as impressive, and the spaghetti with creamy mushroom sauce was absolutely delicious, probably one of the best I’ve had in the area. Everything was presented beautifully and tasted freshly made.

Another big plus is that the café is pet-friendly, allowing customers to bring their dogs along. It’s nice to see how well-behaved and friendly the other guests are, which really adds to the pleasant atmosphere.

If you’re visiting this part of town, Rolls.space is definitely a place you shouldn’t miss. Whether you come for the food, coffee, or just to relax with your pet, it’s the perfect spot to take a break and enjoy some genuinely good vibes.

Dr. Niwech

user_reviews.Description:
This little café in Doi Saket is truly a hidden gem. ☕️
Of course, the coffee is wonderful, but I highly recommend trying the food menu as well — every dish is worth exploring.
My personal favorite is the open-faced mushroom sandwich, full of rich, earthy flavor.
And the cakes… they remind me of the lovely patisseries back home in Japan.
Their shortcake, made with seasonal fresh fruits, fluffy sponge, and light whipped cream, is absolutely divine. 🍓

On Saturday afternoons, you can also enjoy live music that fills the place with an easygoing charm.

There’s parking available, though the space is a bit tight, so when it gets busy, I usually park a little farther away and walk.

user_reviews.Description:
My family of 7 adults and 4 kids below age 6 had the pleasure of staying at this beautiful farm stay for 3 nights.

The owners and staff were very warm and hospitable, provided excellent service and always with a smile.
The food (breakfast/lunch/dinner) is very tasty and affordable. They’re very accommodating to special requests. Special mention to the chicken cordon bleu that was really yummy!
They served a lovely mu kratha dinner one of the nights and the meat were fresh and tasty.

I stayed at the Cave room with a bunk bed and it was a nicely designed room, it was clean and cosy, the atmosphere is wonderful.

You can visit the farm animals and feed them, there is also a nice sand playground for the kids next to the restaurant.

The location is a bit out of the way if you’re not driving your own car, but they can assist you with arranging a van with driver at an affordable price.

I’d recommend to contact them directly to book your accommodation instead of using booking platforms.

title: Phli : Cafe x Khao Soi
address: V22V+WFC Phli : Cafe x Khao Soi, 693 San Sai Luang, San Sai District, Chiang Mai 50210

user_reviews.Description:
We were recommended to try here by some friends and were very happy with our food and drinks in a very nice setting.

I had the Khao Soy Beef which was good, nice flavour and the beef was tender. Portion isn't huge but very reasonable for the price and suitable for a light lunch or brunch. I also enjoyed my beverage which was a sparkling peach rose.

A lot of thought and care has gone into creating this charming Cafe. Nicely decorated both inside and out.
Seating available inside with air-conditioning and plenty of seating outdoors.
We chose to sit outdoors on the day of our visit and despite being a warm day, we were very comfortable in the shade. The staff member that took our order told us to feel free to turn on the fan next to the table if we felt it was warm.

Good little menu that also contains some Korean style food items plus good desert options including fresh cakes and Korean style waffles. We shared a waffle with vanilla ice cream for dessert and found it very nice with the waffle being very crispy.

Plenty of parking on site for both cars and motorcycles and a huge overflow parking lot directly opposite the Cafe. ( Photos included)

A nice atmosphere all round, with friendly staff and good background music both inside and out adding to what was overall an excellent experience.

Recommended and will return again to try some of their other menu items.

user_reviews.Description:
Tasty Tofu and Friendly Atmosphere

I had a nice meal here. The tofu was soft and well prepared with a good touch of curry powder—simple but satisfying. The lady serving was very kind and had a warm, friendly presence, which added to the overall experience.

The tea was surprisingly good—especially the fruit tea. I’d definitely consider coming back just for that.

The restaurant itself could be a bit more organized inside; a little more structure or tidiness would make the space feel more welcoming and comfortable for guests.

As for the dogs, I didn’t see any mistreatment at all. On the contrary, they seemed well cared for and relaxed. It was actually comforting to see how much attention they were given.

Overall, a decent spot with potential to improve—but already worth a visit if you’re a vegetarian.

user_reviews.Description:
This restaurant is an absolute delight! From the moment you step in, you're greeted with warmth by lovely staff, making for a truly welcoming experience.

The food here is simply delicious. They offer an impressive array of Japanese, Western, and Thai dishes, and every single one I've tried has been fantastic. Currently, my personal favorite is their "Tamago-yaki (Japanese-style omelet) set" - it's perfectly prepared and incredibly satisfying.

And don't even get me started on their coffee and bakery items! They're definitely not to be missed. You'll find unique treats like Japanese-style curry bread and shio pan, along with a wonderful selection of sweet pastries.
I highly recommend this charming spot for anyone looking for a memorable meal in Chiang Mai!

In my opinion, the negative aspects of this hotel (particularly in room 02); The ventilation of the inner room is inadequate, the bathroom and its drain need attention, too much air freshener is used throughout the house, causing it to be a stuffy, smelly place and increasing the existing bad smell exponentially. !!! Bed: A bed that feels like a raised mat on an MDF board. Just as we got used to sleeping on a hard bed in this region, we also experienced the hardness of the solid floor :) After the 3 nights we stayed, we did not have any pain due to the place we slept on, so we thought maybe this is a Korean tradition. Apart from these, its location, atmosphere and facilities are more than sufficient, it just needs a little attention.

user_reviews.Description:
If you’re looking for a cozy-ish spot to sip coffee while escaping the crowds, Keane Coffee & Guest House is a hidden gem near Jing Jai Market. With its vintage and hipster decor, stepping inside feels like entering a warm, inviting home. The ambiance is relaxing with nice music in the background, although the lighting leans a bit too warm for our taste.

The seating is well thought out, with options for both work and chilling. We enjoyed their light and medium roast iced lattes, both of which were made well. They also have a good selection of non-caffeinated drinks, making it a great choice for everyone. They also have non-dairy milk options with additional 20 Bahts. The drinks are priced between 60-85 Bahts which is not bad for the air conditioned cafe.

On a second visit, we tried the Thai iced tea, but it was a bit too creamy for our liking, despite its popularity. The butter cake was tasty but on the small side for the price.

Overall, it’s a lovely cafe with friendly owners and a chill vibe, perfect for getting some work done or just unwinding with good music.

Definitely worth checking out!

user_reviews.Description:
A refined yet casual cafe, with scrumptious eggs.

Eggy Eggy offers the best eggs I've had in Chiang Mai, and is generally amongst the top restaurants I've visited here over the past half year. The menu tips offers dishes from Hong Kong, Yunnan, Portuguese, and French cuisine, plus a few more.

I've sampled a dish from most, and they were terrific. The chef here has certain skills- some of the sauces used cannot be made quickly, and were certainly made in-house with care.

The char siu, noodles and eggs (in all preparations, including the noodles) are at the forefront of why I'm so fond of this restaurant. Highly recommended.

user_reviews.Description:
This used to be a great place for a few drinks and a variety of different meats on a stick.

It has changed hands recently, the tables are in disrepair, and the chairs are 80% broken.

There is no table service, which is fine, but nobody will tell you this.

There should be a process where you choose your meat on a stick selection, be given a tally of your choices, so there is no confusion when you go to pay.
This seems logical to me, yet twice since the new people have taken over, my bill has been almost doubled.

It is a real shame, as the right people managing this place could really make it work.

EDIT: Since writing this review, the tables have been replaced, the area is a whole lot nicer.

user_reviews.Description:
I stopped by GAAD Cafe Chiang Mai for a coffee and a light lunch, and it turned out to be one of those places that instantly makes you want to slow down.

The café has a calm, modern atmosphere with a thoughtful design that feels both cozy and inspiring. If you head up to the second floor, you’ll be treated to a lovely view of the old Chiang Mai city wall, which makes the experience even more special and relaxing.

The coffee was smooth, rich, and beautifully prepared, while the light lunch was fresh, flavorful, and just the right portion. Everything was made with care, and the friendly service made the visit even more enjoyable.

If you’re looking for a peaceful café in Chiang Mai with great coffee, delicious food, and a beautiful view, GAAD Cafe is definitely worth a visit. I’ll certainly be back the next time I’m in Chiang Mai.

title: Malee Bakery & Ice Cream
address: 104 Charoen Prathet Rd, Tambon Chang Khlan, เมือง Chiang Mai 50100

user_reviews.Description:
The café is quite small and has only three tables, so the space feels a little cramped, especially when there are several customers. I came here mainly because their coconut cake has been heavily promoted on Instagram, and I was really curious to try it.

Unfortunately, the cake was quite disappointing and didn’t taste as good as I expected. The overall flavor was very mild and lacked the rich coconut taste I was hoping for. The cream was probably the biggest disappointment for me. Instead of tasting like fresh, rich and creamy whipped cream, it had a slightly powdery and gelatin-like texture, as if it had been thickened with a powdered ingredient. It didn’t have that smooth, creamy and indulgent taste you would expect from a good dessert.

The price was also quite high considering the size. The cake cost around 390 baht, which felt expensive for a small cake that was roughly the size of a handful.

Overall, I think the cake is quite Instagram-famous and visually appealing, but for me, the taste and texture did not live up to the hype. The café itself is cute but very limited in seating, with only three tables, so it may not be the best place if you’re looking for a spacious or relaxing café experience. I’m glad I tried it once, but personally, I wouldn’t go out of my way to have it again.

user_reviews.Description:
I was just casually cafe hopping in Chiang Mai and
I stopped at Entheos Coffee Roasters because the name pulled me in... I saw their SCA certifications and thought, okay they are very educated about their coffee.

Ordered my usual in any cafe in CNX -
one specialty drink + my dirty. The coffee was great as expected.

Then I saw a random menu of a burger.
No expectations.
Just hungry so l ordered a Truffle Burger.

It looked simple. A burger with arugula, bacon and a truffled mayo with mushrooms.

I took a bite.
In that instance, my time has slowed down during that first bite.

I never thought I would say this but...

It was THE BEST BURGER IN MY LIFE.

l inhaled it.
Didn't even take a photo because I was so immersed in it.
Which is honestly so criminal on my part.

How did the best burger of my life happen at a random coffee roaster that I passed by randomly???

And I can't believe it. Right when I leave for Bangkok so I won't experience this for awhile.

I just hope it's still there when I come back.
