user_reviews.Description:
The café is beautiful and spacious, with a lovely garden around. You can hear birds chirping, flowers blooming, and I even saw a tiny colorful jumping spider for the first time!

The owner is warm, easygoing, and speaks English fluently. He greets every customer and puts so much care into the homemade food, drinks, and the whole experience. It’s clear the café is his baby. Even on my first visit, I felt like I was visiting a kind relative in Chiang Mai.

The café gets even more beautiful when the sun goes down and the lights come on.
It’s also easy to get a Grab there and back. So I recommend it. You can easily spend a day here relaxing or work on your laptop.

user_reviews.Description:
If you love coffee you’re in for a special treat at Magic Beans! The owner Benz is a true expert in coffee, and he’s got his own coffee roaster in house, so you can buy locally grown fresh artisanal coffee and sample his different blends that he developed. user_reviews.Description:
Wow! The Ours Café ☕️

It’s been a long time since I’ve felt like writing a review — but this place truly deserves it.
From the design and construction details to the care in every material used — it’s absolutely beautiful. You can feel the thought that went into every part of it.

The kids’ books, the play area, the clay walls, and all the wooden tables — everything feels so natural and warm. It’s such a lovely space for children to play and parents to relax.

And what amazed me most — everything is free for the kids to enjoy as long as you buy coffee or food. Many kids’ cafés charge so much just for playtime, but not here.

Drinks start around 60 THB — so reasonable for such a beautiful and mindful place. Honestly, I almost didn’t want to post this because I wanted to keep it my secret spot (especially since Nolan can’t be around too many kids right now).

But this café truly deserves a big shout-out. 💛

user_reviews.Description:
This little corner coffee shop is absolutely one of our favorites in Chiang Mai!
The owner roasts her own coffee every day (which sometimes smells amazing) and grinds it fresh for every coffee drink.
They make some amazing lattes and cappuccinos, but also have a wide variety of other choices.
There is seating on the street level that is open, but if you prefer a quieter place to relax or work, there is a large, air conditioned room upstairs with couches and tables where you can sit and enjoy your time.
Free WiFi is available.
They have coffee and tea drinks, milk drinks, sodas, water, and smoothies, as well as really great danishes, croissants, and desserts. Ice cream is available, too.
Prices are really reasonable for the high quality.
We will keep recommending this little place to all of our friends!

All ingredients used are very tasty. Even the olive oil is of an exceptionally high quality, something that is often lacking in Thailand.
The coffees they serve are all done very well too, sourcing their beans from a couple of well-known local coffee roasters.
Highly recommended!

title: So Into Cafe & Eatery
address: 315, San Sai Noi, San Sai District, Chiang Mai 50210

user_reviews.Description:
• Shrimp Black Ink Pasta: This was the standout for me. The creamy, savory sauce against the black pasta was incredibly rich, and the shrimp were huge and cooked perfectly. Plus, the little yellow flower garnish made it almost too pretty to eat (almost).
• Classic Carbonara: They serve this the "real" way with a raw egg yolk in the middle. Once you mix it in, the sauce becomes super silky and sticks to the pasta perfectly. The crispy bacon on top gives it that much-needed salty crunch.
• Bacon & Dried Chili Spaghetti: A great choice if you want something lighter with a bit of a kick. It’s garlicky, spicy, and topped with some really pretty pink florals.
• The Brunch Sides: We also had a stuffed omelet/quesadilla that was cheesy and golden, plus some toasted baguette with herbed butter that was a great starter.
• The Coffee: You can tell they take their beans seriously. The espresso had a perfect crema and was served on a nice wooden tray with a side of water—very classy.

Kangwan Cafe & Bistro is a cafe in the Saraphi district of Chiang Mai. The owner renovated an old rice barn into a beautiful surrounding coffee shop. There are seating areas both inside the old house and in an air-conditioned extension with plenty of tables. My younger brother said that when the shop first opened, the owner's family welcomed us and cooked all the food themselves. He was very impressed. The menu offers a wide selection of drinks and food, all delicious. He definitely has to find an opportunity to visit again. Today, we came for coffee and dessert while enjoying the beautiful, shady cafe. Photography enthusiasts won't be disappointed, especially on a clear day when the photos are beautiful. Today, I met a customer from Uttaradit who was on business in Chiang Mai and stopped by for coffee and food. I'm delighted. Please come and help promote the local economy and generate income

I understand that is our responsibility to store safely our cash but it was. Somebody with a key came in and opened the closet, then the backpack and browsed through it until the plastic envelope with the money came out, it's not like it was on the bed or else, but its not that, the owner didn't even showed up to talk to us but just sent us to the police and after that moment all the staff was really grumpy with us! At checkout they even tried to keep my key deposit claiming I didn't gave it upon check in! Awful experience absolutely avoid this place

user_reviews.Description: We stayed here for 2 weeks. We travel in Thailand every winter since 2018 . I never had a single problem. So, for one time I decide to go in a place that seems better then the budget ones where we usually go .I was happy  because is a huge space for our standard and it seems safe . I say seems because somebody stole 500 euro from a bag Inside my backpack that I  left in the closet ( I need to change them) . So , I know ilI was stupid and stupid people deserve this sort of things, but actually I didn't expect this because I always praise this country for his kind and honest People. Long story short , they say they don't know anything about ( of course) but nobody broke in the apartment  so I let you guess what you want. They send me to the police but I mean ... I did it just because I didn't know what else to do . So don't be stupid and trusty like me. Stay safe.

user_reviews.Description:
One of the best petting zoos I have seen; not only is the area clean, not smelly, well maintained and properly staffed, but the animals are also in good conditions. A lot of time the pigs look like they are abandoned, but here in Uncle Pong’s they look very happy and the shows provide them with a good opportunity to walk around.

That being said, the baby pigs and baby goats are absolutely adorable and they actually smell so good. Being able to hand feed them MILK at a more than reasonable price, this is one of the loveliest experiences I have had. Also, the staff are very friendly and you can tell they love their job. Overall, an amazing experience.

I hope I will see people drinking from reusable glasses in the future.

Warm regards,
Cat 🙏

user_reviews.Description:
A Hidden Gem in Chiang Mai: Living Room Coffee Shop

Living Room Coffee Shop is an absolute delight and quickly became one of my favorite spots in Chiang Mai. Nestled away from the hustle and bustle, this café is a serene escape with a unique charm that sets it apart from the rest.

First and foremost, the coconut smoothie is nothing short of spectacular. It's rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced — an absolute must-try for anyone visiting. Pair it with their delicious snacks or coffee, and you’ve got yourself a winning combo.

The staff are warm, welcoming, and always ready with a smile. They truly make the experience feel special, adding to the relaxing and friendly atmosphere of the café.

But perhaps the most unique and delightful feature is the gang of four adorable bunnies that roam in their little enclosure! These furry companions add a whimsical touch to the café’s vibe. Watching them hop around is a soothing and oddly entertaining experience. It got me wondering — what is the difference between a bunny and a rabbit? And while we’re at it, what do you call a group of rabbits? (Someone tell me so I can stop calling them a “gang” — though it suits them perfectly!)

Whether you're looking for a quiet spot to relax, a place to work, or just craving a great coconut smoothie in Chiang Mai, Living Room Coffee Shop is an absolute must-visit. I’ll definitely be coming back for the vibes, the drinks, and of course, to visit my bunny friends!

title: LANN Cafe'
address: LANN Cafe' 12 Bunrueang Rit Rd, Suthep, เมือง Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
Lann – where coffee meets calm and excellent taste in design

Lann is one of those rare little cafés that feels intentionally beautiful without trying too hard. Tucked right in front of a hotel spa (yes, that kind of vibe), it’s the perfect spot to decompress before or after pretending you live a slower, more elegant life.

There’s easy parking (already winning), and once inside, you immediately feel how much care the owners put into every detail. The space blends classic Thai rattan textures with clean, modern architecture, creating a mood that’s equal parts cozy, stylish, and quietly luxurious. It’s the kind of place where you sit down and instantly lower your voice without knowing why.

Great coffee, calm energy, and an atmosphere that makes you want to stay longer than planned—whether you’re post-spa, pre-meeting, or just escaping Bangkok chaos for a moment.

Highly recommended if you appreciate good design, thoughtful spaces, and cafés that feel like a small retreat rather than just another caffeine stop

I highly recommend this cafe to anyone looking for great quality and a welcoming vibe. I’ll definitely be back!

user_reviews.Description:
I love this café a lot.
You can have breakfast, lunch, or brunch there until around 3:30–4:00 PM. The place feels like a combination of different shops.
You order everything at the café first, then sit anywhere you like.

I didn’t see any air-conditioned indoor area, but the outdoor atmosphere was quite comfortable — the weather was slightly rainy, and the space is surrounded by lots of greenery.

It’s also okay to do remote work upstairs for around 3–4 hours. It’s not crowded at all, which makes it even better.
Plus, there’s a separate and lovely gift shop where you can buy some Burmese traditional products.

Highly recommended if you enjoy a peaceful vibe.

user_reviews.Description:
Folklosophy Cafe: A Tranquil Escape in San Sai's Green Embrace
Folklosophy Cafe in San Sai, Chiang Mai, is more than just a coffee shop; it's a delightful escape that blends charming aesthetics with a wonderfully relaxed atmosphere. Tucked away amidst lush greenery, it offers a serene retreat from the bustling city, making it a perfect spot for anyone seeking a peaceful moment or a quiet place to work.
One of the most immediate draws of Folklosophy Cafe is its ambiance. Described by many as having a Japanese or Muji-inspired style, the cafe exudes a minimalist yet warm and inviting feel. The natural light filtering in, combined with the thoughtful decor, creates a tranquil environment that encourages slow living and appreciation for the surroundings. What truly sets it apart, however, is the panoramic view of rice fields and mountains that greets you. Imagine sipping your coffee while gazing out at vast, emerald green fields, with the distant peaks creating a picturesque backdrop. This, coupled with the gentle breeze, makes for an incredibly calming and refreshing experience. It's an ideal spot for those looking to unwind, read a book, or simply enjoy nature's beauty.
While the exact "recommended" menu items can vary with personal preference, Folklosophy Cafe is consistently praised for its excellent coffee and fresh baked goods. Reviewers often highlight the quality of their coffee, with many mentioning a preference for their medium roast. Beyond coffee, they offer a good selection of non-coffee drinks, including teas and Italian sodas, catering to a variety of tastes. When it comes to treats, the cafe is particularly known for its tasty cakes and extensive menu of baked goods. While specific names are not widely advertised as "best sellers," the general consensus points to their pastries as a highlight, perfect for pairing with your chosen beverage.
Beyond the delicious offerings, the cafe's key selling points extend to its unique features. Firstly, it is a pet-friendly cafe, which is a huge bonus for those traveling with their furry companions. They even have a large, fenced lawn, providing ample space for dogs to run around and play freely, making it a truly inclusive spot for animal lovers. Secondly, despite its slightly "hidden" location (often described as being a bit off the main road, through cornfields), it's easily navigable with GPS, and this sense of discovery only adds to its charm. It feels like a secret gem waiting to be found. For students from Maejo University, it's a popular choice for studying or working, thanks to the ample seating and available power outlets. The reasonable pricing for both food and drinks also makes it an attractive option for regular visits.
In conclusion, Folklosophy Cafe is a true find in San Sai. It's a place where the simple pleasures of good coffee, delicious treats, and a breathtaking natural setting converge to create an unforgettable experience. Whether you're a local seeking a new favorite haunt or a traveler looking for a serene escape, Folklosophy Cafe offers a unique blend of tranquility, quality, and hospitality that makes it well worth the visit. It's a place where you can truly slow down, breathe, and appreciate the beauty of Chiang Mai.

title: Cafe Leng Doi Pui
address: Suthep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
This place is a hidden gem in Doi Pui Hmong village. As it is located bit away from the main tourist area (you need to walk about 200m) to get to this place. It has basic cottages (about 6, I think) on various ground levels. Although I had only a meal at this place, I am sure it is a nice experience to stay in one of these cottages.
The food was delicious, and well-presented authentic Hmong food. Food is freshly prepared using local ingredients. You immediately see the difference between pre-prepared food and freshly prepared food.
The owner and his wife are very friendly. You can sit at the open-air dining area at the top part of the property with an amazing view over the valley.
There are only very small direction signs (name and how to get to this place) at the centre part of the village and that could be the reason that it is not known to visitors.

user_reviews.Description:
The cake shop at Dhara Dhevi truly lives up to its reputation! 🍰✨ Their macarons are absolutely delicious, with over 20 flavors available. Unfortunately, when we visited, only 4 flavors were in stock — which was a bit disappointing because we were hoping to try more.

That said, the White Truffle macaron completely stole the show! It tasted just like a warm truffle mushroom soup — incredibly unique and flavorful. Another standout was the chocolate caramel tart — the perfect balance of rich, dark chocolate bitterness and just the right amount of caramel sweetness. It was divine.

The staff were very polite and attentive, making us feel welcome from the moment we walked in. The atmosphere is cozy, elegant, and perfect for an afternoon tea experience. The shop also offers a selection of fine teas — I tried the Pure Chamomile, and it was absolutely delightful.

Overall, it’s a lovely spot to treat yourself with premium pastries, enjoy a relaxing tea time, and soak in a warm, peaceful ambiance. Highly recommended! 🌿🫖🍫

user_reviews.Description:
While the macaroons are delicious—seriously well made , if you find yourself heading to a hot spring definitely stop here.

A beautiful abandoned resort, appears to have shut down since Covid but was a 60 acre super high end luxury (and I mean like; you’d have to have had some generational wealth to have stayed here) hotel built to resemble an ancient palace (we were so convinced it’s an old palace in ruins we were shocked to learn it was a hotel, imagining just the cost to create such a place in modern day) now over grown with wild greenery and slowly decaying away its sadly mostly closed to visitors.

The bakery is a reason to stop, the restrooms are also very clean so a nice place to stop even for a break to stretch the legs. but you’ll find yourself drawn into nature and the abandoned hotel. While visitors aren’t allowed security is pretty lax and on a lazy afternoon one could attempt to sneak in for a peek.

Would go back just to explore as what we saw obviously wasn’t even a smidge of the 60 acres laying inside in waste.

All that stands now is this bakery all other stores are shut down, would go back just to explore the grounds — and grab a macaroon too 🤭

Pictures don’t do it justice, just stop by if you’re passing it.

title: BabyBunny คาเฟ่กระต่าย
address: 118, San Sai Noi, San Sai District, Chiang Mai 50210

user_reviews.Description:
Amazing rabbit cafe with incredible service!
I visited last Thursday but the shop was closed due to a power outage. To make up for the inconvenience, the staff kindly gave me a free coffee today — such thoughtful customer service that totally won me over.

You only need to order a cup of coffee to play with rabbits, no extra entrance fee at all. There are 9 lively, friendly bunnies here. A small cup of rabbit feed grass costs only 20 THB, which lasts for ages to feed and interact with the little cuties.

The space is spotlessly clean, and staff swap out rabbits regularly so you can spend time with many different bunnies. All rabbits are super active and gentle to touch.

Their drinks look stunning and taste fantastic! They also have great kids’ meals with freshly cooked fries and shrimp tempura, perfect for family outings with children.
100% recommend for anyone looking for a relaxing, kid-friendly spot in Chiang Mai!

title: Nebaker cafe
address: 107 Nebaker cafe 1, San Pu Loei, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
There is something deeply inviting about a space curated with intention. This cafe captures a "warm, simple, old touch" perfectly, reflecting the owner’s clear passion for Japan and authentic vintage finds. Every corner feels like a curated gallery of Japanese history, filled with used items that give the venue a soul you won't find in modern, minimalist chains. It’s the kind of place where the environment encourages you to slow down and appreciate the craftsmanship of a bygone era.
While the interior design is nearly flawless, the only thing that could possibly elevate the experience further would be a view of a lush rice field to match the peaceful indoor vibe. That said, the atmosphere remains incredibly cozy and restorative.
The service is another high point—the staff are genuinely friendly and provide a welcoming energy from the moment you walk in. I opted for a Chai Yen (Thai Milk Tea) this time; it was a solid, dependable drink, though perhaps not the standout of the menu. However, seeing the selection of desserts on display convinced me that a return trip is necessary. Next time, the cakes are definitely at the top of my list. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates rustic Japanese aesthetics.

user_reviews.Description:
In my opinion, Joko Bakery is the best all-around bakery in Thailand, and I've invested measurable effort toward finding good bakeries.

Joe, the Austrian founder and Chief Baking Dude, and his partner Ae craft and share exceptional breads, pastries, quiches, cakes, cookies, and more. They also have flourless breads.

We discovered they deliver country-wide, supply restaurants and coffee shops in Chiang Mai, have a street-side presence Sunday mornings at Brewing Room in Chiang Mai, and are opening their new bakery location at a farm in Mae Rim.

They are principled business owners, very friendly community members, and expert craftsmen.

If you are in Chiang Mai and love proper croissants made with real butter or fancy a range of other tasty baked wonders, I highly recommend you swing by.

user_reviews.Description:
Dropped by Dee Cafe and was pleasantly surprised. Their coffee is really aromatic, smooth and strong enough to perk you up. I had the orange Americano—the coffee is quite intense, but it is to my liking. If you prefer something lighter, you can actually ask them to adjust with less coffee and more fresh orange juice—they’re happy to tweak it for your taste.

The raisin Danish puff pastry was nicely done—crispy outside, soft inside, not too sweet, just right.

But the one that really stood out was the coconut cake. Super soft, moist, and topped with a thick layer of coconut cream with actual coconut flesh inside. It’s rich but not jelak—seriously good!

The cafe itself is cozy and comfortable, perfect spot to chill. I think travellers will find this place worth visiting, especially with their unique drinks and dessert options. Highly recommend trying the ones I mentioned!

It was a pleasure to stay at Starbarks Cafe! Our 3 dogs were more than happy, so did us!

First of all, I really appreciate the hospitality of the staff and owner. I really feel that people love their business and services they provide, cause service was exceptional!

Also we received a discount for the second and third dog 👍
Thank you once again! It was great experience 🩷
Really recommend!

(Photo and video were made by staff during our dogs stay 👏💕)

user_reviews.Description:
They have wide variety of coffee options, with most drinks priced around 50–60 baht, which is very reasonable. The staff prepared my coffee right in front of me with impressive efficiency, and the whole process felt smooth and professional.

You can drink inside, but the space is a bit small, so it’s more of a cozy, quick-stop kind of café. That said, the compact size actually adds to its charm—the shop has a simple, cute atmosphere that feels very local.

A great spot if you’re looking for affordable, good-quality coffee near the university area.

user_reviews.Description:
It is difficult to describe this place, as it is more than a café/restaurant. There are multiple buildings, tastefully decorated with traditional Indian decor by highlighting its rich colors, handcrafted furniture and decorative accents. There is also an area front of the restaurant/café with old timer motorcycles (including at least one Harely Davidson old timer), couple of old timer Massy Ferguson tractors.

I only had a coffee here as my visit was not planned. I had lunch at a nearby Sukhothai Noodle restaurant and the service personal there mentioned about this place underlining the Indian decorations.

This Café/Restaurant can be compared to a gallery or a specific art movement, and highlight elements like architectural design, color palettes, and unique installations.

The coffee was very good and service was friendly.

user_reviews.Description:
Today, I took one of my drives out of town to an amazing coffee shop situated on a rice farm about 50 to 60 minutes away from home depending on traffic, and honestly, well worth the drive even if it took an hour and a half, lol.

The place is built in a traditional Thai wooden style, with mostly open-air spaces some elevated, some right out on the grass, all overlooking the rice fields. There’s also a small air-conditioned indoor room if you prefer a cooler spot. The atmosphere was serene and peaceful.

They offer a delightful selection of coffees, teas, and other drinks, along with a tempting array of pastries and more. I had a pot of ginger tea (with honey, of course) and the best cheesecake I’ve had outside of New York.

Out there, I could hear nothing but birds and bugs, how refreshing is that, I sat outside overlooking the rice field. I’ll admit it was a bit warm for hot ginger tea, but not unbearable. I can only imagine how perfect it must be in the cooler months, and I’ll definitely be back to find out.

I’ve shared just a few snapshot here, they have tons of photos, this is definitely one of the nicest cafés I’ve ever visited. It even made me think about moving somewhere more peaceful like this. There are plenty of hidden gems like it if you’re willing to drive a bit to find them.

user_reviews.Description:
The Chiang Mai Rooftop Bar: Awesome place to be!

Nestled in the heart of the city, Hide Land is one of Chiang Mai's most captivating "secret" rooftop bars. Known for its chic, industrial-meets-minimalist ambiance, it offers a sophisticated yet relaxed escape from the bustling streets below.

The highlight of any visit is undoubtedly the rooftop restaurant, which provides an excellent 360-degree view of the surrounding urban landscape. As the evening approaches, the space transforms; it is a prime destination for sunset enthusiasts, with dozens of people flocking here daily to catch the golden hour. The sight of the sun dipping behind the lush green hills and the iconic Doi Suthep mountain range is nothing short of breathtaking.

Beyond the scenery, Hide Land has built a stellar reputation for its culinary and mixology offerings. The cocktails are the true stars—famous for being expertly balanced and creatively presented. Whether you prefer a classic or a signature Thai-inspired infusion, the drinks are as impressive as the vista. Complementing the bar is a menu of high-quality food that elevates the experience from a simple drink spot to a full dining destination. For anyone seeking a trendy atmosphere and a million-dollar view, Hide Land is an absolute must-visit place

title: Ccccc CAFE
address: 6 Ccccc CAFE, 11 Nimmanhemin Rd Nimmanhaemin Tambon Su Thep, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai 50200

user_reviews.Description:
Wonderful atmosphere and a very convenient location, just a short walk from Maya, One Nimman, and Think Park. Every table is equipped with a power outlet, and the café is open until 9 p.m., making it an excellent place to study or work. There’s also a hostel on the upper floor, which makes it a great option for travelers.

They serve good coffee ⭐️⭐️⭐️ , delicious desserts, and excellent food at reasonable prices. The restroom is also clean and well maintained.
(You can also order beer and wine 🍷 and enjoy the lovely Nimman street view!)

The staff are friendly, welcoming, and have a great sense of humor, which made my visit even more enjoyable. The customers are also polite and respectful

and, as a bonus, they’re quite good-looking. 🙂‍↔️

Overall, this café offers a comfortable and relaxing environment that makes it easy to spend hours here. It’s definitely one of those places you’ll want to come back to again and again.

user_reviews.Description:
Coffee Waan: A Hidden Gem That Redefines Refreshment

In the bustling heart of Chiang Mai, where charming cafes abound, Coffee Waan stands out as an oasis of perfection—a tiny but mighty temple of taste. I stopped here for an Italian soda, having wisely decided it was too late in the day for coffee (a rare but necessary concession to my caffeine sensitivity). What I encountered was nothing short of extraordinary.

Let’s start with the Italian soda. Sure, it’s a simple beverage by nature, but here, it transcends its humble origins. Served not in the soulless confines of plastic but in a mason jar, this drink radiates class and authenticity. There is an inexplicable joy in sipping something served in real glass—it tastes better, feels better, and simply is better. The mason jar was a stroke of genius, a nod to rustic charm that perfectly aligns with the cafe's vibe. I felt like I was drinking the elixir of life.

The space itself is a cozy haven of charm. Every inch of this tiny cafe feels curated with love. The seating is snug and intimate, the lighting warm and inviting. The playlist? Absolute perfection. It's the kind of background music that makes you feel like the star of your own independent film, sitting there with your mason jar of soda, contemplating life's mysteries or maybe just the refreshing taste of your drink.

The staff? Attentive without being overbearing, radiating that rare combination of professionalism and warmth. Their smiles alone could power the cafe’s charm for a week.

To say Coffee Waan is worth a visit would be an understatement. Whether you’re here for coffee or for an impeccably served Italian soda, it’s an experience that reminds you that life’s pleasures are often found in the smallest details—like a mason jar that turns a simple drink into an unforgettable moment.

user_reviews.Description:
I was looking for a cafe with outlets to spend my last afternoon in Chiang Mai (forgot my portable battery pack in Bangkok 😭) and Press continue was perfectly suited for my needs! It wasn’t my original plan but I saw it on Google Maps and thought it would be a good fit because I’m a big gamer.
Coolest little cafe ever and I’m glad I stopped by! Super geeked to be able to try out some old-school NES games, and spent like 2-3 hours trying to beat Super Mario 3 to no avail. That game is harder than it looks! There were a few modern consoles too, though I didn’t try them. The owner’s wife was sweet and helpful, and it didn’t feel like there was any rush at all. Sabai maak maaaaak!
The owner’s collection is extensive and amazing to browse.
I got a Thai tea (45 baht), good price, refreshing and yummy to drink while gaming. Unfortunately no food offerings, which would’ve made this perfect cafe even more perfect.

I was looking for a cafe with outlets to spend my last afternoon in Chiang Mai (forgot my portable battery pack in Bangkok 😭) and Press continue was perfectly suited for my needs! It wasn’t my original plan but I saw it on Google Maps and thought it would be a good fit because I’m a big gamer.
Coolest little cafe ever and I’m glad I stopped by! Super geeked to be able to try out some old-school NES games, and spent like 2-3 hours trying to beat Super Mario 3 to no avail. That game is harder than it looks! There were a few modern consoles too, though I didn’t try them. The owner’s wife was sweet and helpful, and it didn’t feel like there was any rush at all. Sabai maak maaaaak!
The owner’s collection is extensive and amazing to browse.
I got a Thai tea (45 baht), good price, refreshing and yummy to drink while gaming. Unfortunately no food offerings, which would’ve made this perfect cafe even more perfect.

In conclusion: highly recommend, if you’re a casual or avid gamer and looking for good drinks and games while on your way back to the city from the mountain temples!

title: Heyday Cafe @ Chiangmai
address: Rattanakosin Rd, Wat Ket, Meaung, Chiang Mai 50000

user_reviews.Description: Great little cafe offering a wide variety of Thai rice and noodle dishes and a small selection of western breakfast options at very friendly prices. I opted for the English breakfast, two eggs, three small sausages and toast. At 65 baht it represented great value, and I absolutely loved the thick sliced toast. The coffee was excellent too, capuccino costing just 45 baht. I noticed they had crepes in the fridge, strawberry, chocolate banana, chocolate Oreo or plain. I ordered a strawberry to eat in and chocolate banana to take out, both delicious, in particular the strawberry. These would cost 150 baht or more in the west but here only 35 baht, wow! Heyday Cafe has that industrial look inside, is spotlessly clean, comfortable seating, AC and staff who are welcoming, even though their English language skills are limited. If you are in the area and in need of a feed or a coffee fix then this is the place to go.

user_reviews.Description:
While exploring the old town, randomly bumped into this cool looking coffee stand on the road a few weeks ago and finally got a chance to try it today. My girlfriend and I were not disappointed.

The quality of the coffee beans aroma and taste were quite strong and flavourful. They used a small hand grinder and after dripped the coffee into the cup. This artistic and organic coffee stand is quite unique. Try smelling a sample of the beans and give it a try! Prices are quite decent as well if you want hot or cold drinks.

Strike up a conversation with the owners (Thai and a lady from Hong Kong), they are quite nice as well and can tell you a little bit about the coffee. Highly recommend this place if you're in the area.

​สวัสดีค่ะทุกคน วันนี้ Phurita พาเพลิน จะพาทุกคนมาเช็คอินร้าน "เฉยชา คาเฟ่"

คาเฟ่เปิดใหม่แกะกล่องที่กำลังมาแรงมากๆ รอบนี้พากลุ่มเพื่อนและเด็กๆ มาลองชิมเมนูของหวานและเครื่องดื่มกันค่ะ ขอบอกเลยว่ารีวิวนี้พลีชีพสุดๆ ดีก็ชม ตรงไหนไม่รอดเราก็บอกกันตรงๆ แบบสุภาพ เพื่อให้ทุกคนเอาไปประกอบการตัดสินใจกันน้า รอบนี้ขอให้คะแนนภาพรวมไว้ที่ 3 ดาวค่ะ มาดูรีวิวเจาะลึกกันเลย!

​🟢 จุดที่ประทับใจ (ดีงามชวนลอง)
​ปังปิ้งหน้าล้นๆ ทำดีทำถึง: เมนูขนมปังปิ้งทำออกมาได้ดีทีเดียวค่ะ ตัวเด็ดคือ ปังปิ้งหน้าพิซซ่าชีส อบมาได้กรอบนอกนุ่มใน ท็อปปิ้งซอสและไส้กรอกมาแบบฉ่ำสะใจ ส่วน ปังปิ้งเนยนม ก็หอมมันหวานกำลังดี ทานคู่กับเครื่องดื่มถือว่าเข้ากันได้ดีเลยค่ะ
​เครื่องดื่มหลากหลาย สายชาไทยห้ามพลาด: เมนูเครื่องดื่มมีให้เลือกเยอะมาก โดยเฉพาะกลุ่ม ชากลิ่นอายปักษ์ใต้ และ ชาไทยเฉยชาครีมชีส รสชาติเข้มข้น หอมละมุน ชื่นใจสุดๆ
​มุมถ่ายรูปสไตล์ญี่ปุ่นสุดปัง: หน้าร้านตกแต่งน่ารักมาก มีมุมทางม้าลาย ป้ายสถานีรถไฟญี่ปุ่น และป้ายกูลิโกะยอดฮิต ให้ฟีลเหมือนอยู่ญี่ปุ่นจริงๆ เด็กๆ เดินแบบถ่ายรูปเล่นกันสนุกมาก ถือเป็นจุดขายที่ดีมากๆ ของร้านเลยค่ะ
​🔴 จุดที่ไม่ค่อยประทับใจ (อยากให้ทางร้านปรับปรุง)
​เมนูเยอะจนสับสน ลายตาไปหมด: เมนูของทางร้าน ตรงหน้าเคาว์เตอร์ ค่อนข้างหนาแน่นและซับซ้อนเกินไปหน่อยนึงค่ะ วางสลับไปมาทำให้คนสั่งแอบสับสนและลายตากว่าจะเลือกได้แต่ละเมนู

​บรรยากาศภายในร้านยังไม่ชวนนั่ง: กลิ่นน้ำหอมปรับอากาศด้านในร้านแอบฉุนแรงเกินไปนิดนึงค่ะ นั่งนานๆ แล้วแอบเวียนหัว รวมไปถึงพนักงานในร้านคุยกันเสียงดังค่อนข้างมาก ทำให้บรรยากาศการนั่งทานด้านในดูไม่ค่อยผ่อนคลายเท่าไหร่ (นั่งแล้วแอบไม่ค่อยสนุกค่ะ) ถ้าปรับปรุงเรื่องกลิ่นและการควบคุมเสียงของพนักงานได้จะน่าชั่งยาวๆ กว่านี้มากเลย

​📋 ข้อมูลร้านและพิกัดการเดินทาง
​💰 ระดับราคา: ราคามาตรฐานคาเฟ่ทั่วไปเลยค่ะ เมนูขนมปังปิ้งเริ่มต้นที่ 49 - 89 บาท ส่วนเมนูสลอปปี้คลายร้อนและเครื่องดื่มชาต่างๆ เริ่มต้นประมาณ 49 - 99 บาท ถือว่าราคาจับต้องได้ค่ะ

​⏰ เวลาเปิด - ปิด: เปิดให้บริการทุกวัน ตั้งแต่เวลา 10:00 น. – 21:00 น.
​📍 ปักหมุดพิกัด: เฉยชา คาเฟ่ Choei Cha Cafe สามารถเปิด GPS นำทางมาได้เลย ร้านตกแต่งสไตล์มินิมอลญี่ปุ่นเด่นชัดเจน มีที่จอดรถหน้าร้านรองรับสะดวกสบายค่ะ

user_reviews.text_translated:
🍞🧋 Honest Review of "Chuey Cha Cafe": A Japanese-style cafe with a great vibe...but with a few things to be suspicious about?

Hello everyone! Today, Phurita is taking you to check out "Chuey Cha Cafe,"

a brand new cafe that's currently very popular. This time, I brought a group of friends and kids to try their desserts and drinks. Let me tell you, this review is a complete honest review. I'll praise what's good and tell you what's not so good in a polite way, so you can make your own decision. Overall, I'm giving it a 3-star rating. Let's get into the in-depth review!

🟢 Things that impressed me (worth trying):
Overflowing Toast: The toast menu is really well-made. The highlight is the pizza cheese toast, baked crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, topped with a generous amount of sauce and sausage. The butter and milk toast is fragrant, creamy, and just the right amount of sweetness. It pairs well with drinks.
Diverse Drinks - Thai Tea Lovers Can't Miss: There's a wide variety of drinks to choose from, especially the Southern Thai-inspired teas and the Chuey Cha Cream Cheese Thai Tea. Rich flavor, fragrant and incredibly refreshing!
Super cute Japanese-style photo spots: The storefront is decorated adorably, featuring a crosswalk, a Japanese train station sign, and the popular Glico sign, giving you the feeling of being in Japan. Kids will have so much fun taking pictures here. It's a great selling point for the shop.
🔴 Things I didn't like (Things the shop should improve):
Confusing and overwhelming menu: The menu at the counter is quite dense and complicated. The items are jumbled together, making it confusing and overwhelming to choose from.

Uninviting atmosphere: The air freshener scent inside the shop is a bit too strong. Sitting for a long time can make you feel dizzy. Also, the staff are talking quite loudly, making the atmosphere less relaxing (it wasn't very enjoyable). If they could improve the scent and control the staff's noise, it would be much more pleasant to dine there.

📋 Shop Information and Directions
💰 Price Level: Standard cafe prices. Toast starts at 49-89 baht. Slushies and various tea drinks are also available at higher prices. Starting at around 49-99 baht, the prices are quite affordable.

⏰ Opening Hours: Open daily from 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM.
📍 Location: Choei Cha Cafe. You can use GPS navigation to find it. The cafe has a distinctive Japanese minimalist style and convenient parking in front of the shop.

user_reviews.Description:
Visited Starbucks Reserve Nimman Soi 3 for a quick stop while looking for a Starbucks Thailand mug as a souvenir, and it turned out to be a really pleasant experience.

Compared to some busier Starbucks locations, this branch had a much quieter and more relaxing atmosphere, which made it a nice place to take a short break from walking around the area. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the service was smooth and efficient even for a quick visit.

One of the best things about this location is how convenient it is if you’re exploring One Nimman. It’s easy to stop by before shopping, after exploring, or even in between stores if you need a quick caffeine fix or just want to cool down for a bit.

The store itself was clean, comfortable, and well-maintained, with a calm ambiance that made the visit enjoyable. I was also happy to find the Thailand mug I was looking for, which made the stop even more worth it.

Overall, this is a great Starbucks Reserve location to relax for a while if you’re around the Nimman area, especially for travelers looking for souvenirs or a quieter coffee break.

user_reviews.Description:
I came to SoSoulful Café specifically for brunch, but I didn’t realize they’re under new management and no longer serve a brunch menu. They now specialize in Japanese cuisine, so just a heads up if you’re coming in with breakfast expectations like I did (I was definitely in the mood for eggs Benedict 😅).
That said, the food I tried was good. The cheesecake itself wasn’t very sweet, but the strawberry sauce balanced it out nicely. The coconut coffee was just okay—not bad, but not something I’d go out of my way for again.
The highlight for me was the atmosphere. It was incredibly peaceful, the kind of place where you can sit, breathe, and just be. There’s a phrase there, “I will give you rest,” and honestly, you can feel that. I was able to sit and get some writing done without distraction, which I really appreciated.
The owners were also kind and welcoming, which added to the experience.
Overall, while it wasn’t what I expected menu-wise, it turned out to be a calm and pleasant place to spend time. I am definitely going back!

user_reviews.Description: I love the setting of yellow cafe.  All the desert are so good!  Buying sourdough bread becomes the weekly routine for every Sunday morning, about 9:30, fresh backed sourdough breads are available at cafe. user_reviews.Description:
We first read about this café in the September 2025 edition of Bangkok Air magazine, where it was featured as an upcoming and highly recommended coffee spot. It’s tucked away in a rather unexpected location—inside a warehouse-style area surrounded by car servicing garages, skate rinks, and workshops.

The café itself is small but thoughtfully designed, with a cozy and cute interior. What truly stood out, though, was the coffee. We tried the Young Style and Berry Bomb Americano, and both were outstanding. The preparation was meticulous—down to precise milligram measurements—which really showed in the flavor.

A hidden little gem for coffee lovers. 😊☕

user_reviews.Description:
This review is strictly for the cafe itself, not the pool/onsen.

Forget about going here to work. Probably not even to hang out and chill. Plenty of other places for that. It's clearly not the place for either.
I don't think it even knows what it wants to be. It's really dark and loud, in stark contrast to the entire property around it. Plus it doesn't serve food!

This cafe really should be redesigned to complement the pool/ "onsen" business.

The chairs are super uncomfortable, and the tables are tiny.
The music was very loud too, and the Cafe had most of its blinds down so they can play some really out of place cartoon projected onto the wall. No idea what they are thinking.

I got the "energy" smoothie which was absolutely terrible. It was really small for the price (120, +20 for almond milk,) and it came out as a thick slush that you need a spoon for (which they didn't give). It tasted like a bag of cacao blended with a couple ice cubes. Pretty gross and not what was expected.

Hard pass on this place. Wifi was good and nice view of the pool though.

user_reviews.Description:
Mitbury (the House of Bunnag) is run by a lovely couple, Chinnamit (Mit) Bunnag and his lovely wife Oom (Apisara Javewong). Both came from respectable noble family background in which Mit family purchased this splendid plot of land by Mae Sa stream which flows down the mountain range of Mae Rim district above and by the beautiful curvy road to hidden Samoeng District amongst sea of mountain. The property has been serving as the Noble Bunnag family retreat home for decades and received numerous respectable guests over the time, but most important people amongst them were, there majesties the late King Bhumipol Rama, the 9th, his Queen consort Queen Sirikit, the Crowned Princess Sirindhorn that paid private royal visits for numbers of time.  At present, Mit as a skilful chef who grew up in the UK decided to rearrange the landscape and found his new Cafe & Bistro known as Mitbury to share his wonderful aspects of his life from the history of the place, the people, the food, the well selected coffee beans and friendly spirit of his home amongst one of the most popular natural site of Chiang Mai. Should you travel to Mae Rim on this road to Samoeng for Mae Sa elephant sanctuary, Queen Sirikit Botanical Garden or Mon Cham summit, Mitbury is a must stop for coffee, relaxing by stream, or simply for lovely conversation with Mit and Oom.

Highly recommended ❤️❤️❤️

user_reviews.Description:
If you're looking for a charming and intimate dining experience in Maerim, I highly recommend paying a visit to the delightful owner-operated restaurant tucked away in the heart of the city. This little gem offers an exceptional Vietnamese culinary experience that is worth the wait, as the owner pours her heart and soul into every dish she prepares.

From the moment you step inside, you'll be captivated by the cozy atmosphere and the welcoming smile of the owner. The restaurant's small size adds to its charm, creating an intimate and personal dining experience that is hard to find elsewhere. The owner, who operates the restaurant single-handedly, ensures that every customer feels valued and well taken care of.

The menu at this Vietnamese eatery is a testament to the owner's dedication to authenticity and quality. Each dish is prepared with meticulous attention to detail, using the freshest ingredients available. Whether you're a fan of classic Vietnamese dishes like pho, banh mi, or spring rolls, or if you're looking to explore lesser-known Vietnamese specialties, this restaurant has you covered.

One bite into the food, and you'll immediately taste the love and care that goes into each dish. The flavors are vibrant, the spices are well-balanced, and the presentation is visually appealing. The pho, in particular, is a standout dish, with a rich and aromatic broth that will transport you straight to the streets of Vietnam. And don't forget to try the banh mi, which is crafted with a perfect balance of crispy baguette, savory fillings, and fresh herbs.

While it's true that the food may take a little longer to arrive at your table due to the owner's meticulous preparation process, the wait is well worth it. In a world where fast-food chains dominate, this restaurant offers a refreshing change of pace. It's a place where time seems to slow down, allowing you to savor each moment and truly appreciate the artistry that goes into every dish.

In conclusion, if you're in Maerim and craving a taste of Vietnam, this small owner-operated restaurant is an absolute must-visit. The combination of heartfelt hospitality, authentic flavors, and a cozy ambiance creates an unforgettable dining experience. So take the time, indulge in the delicious food, and allow yourself to be transported to the vibrant streets of Vietnam, right here in Maerim.

If you're in the Panghai area and looking for a cozy coffee shop to relax and enjoy a high-quality cup of coffee, then "Goodvibes Weather Cafe" is definitely worth a visit. The shop is located in the Thepsadej area, which is a nice and peaceful place to spend some time.

For me, one of the highlights of this cafe is their ice espresso, which is simply amazing. It's made with high-quality coffee beans and is perfectly balanced in terms of flavor and strength. Whether you like your coffee strong or mild, you'll definitely find the ice espresso at Goodvibes to your liking.

The cafe itself has a very welcoming and comfortable atmosphere. The decor is simple yet charming, and the staff are friendly and attentive. The seating area is spacious and there are plenty of power outlets available for those who need to work on their laptops.

Overall, I highly recommend Goodvibes for anyone looking for a great coffee shop experience in the Panghai area.

This is a one of my favour coffee shop around here and their ice espresso is a must-try, and you're sure to enjoy the friendly atmosphere and comfortable seating. Give it a try and see for yourself why this cafe is so highly regarded by coffee lovers in the area.

CaffeineThepsadej

For me, one of the highlights of this cafe is their ice espresso, which is simply amazing. It's made with high-quality coffee beans and is perfectly balanced in terms of flavor and strength. Whether you like your coffee strong or mild, you'll definitely find the ice espresso at Goodvibes to your liking.

The cafe itself has a very welcoming and comfortable atmosphere. The decor is simple yet charming, and the staff are friendly and attentive. The seating area is spacious and there are plenty of power outlets available for those who need to work on their laptops.

Overall, I highly recommend Goodvibes for anyone looking for a great coffee shop experience in the Panghai area.

This is a one of my favour coffee shop around here and their ice espresso is a must-try, and you're sure to enjoy the friendly atmosphere and comfortable seating. Give it a try and see for yourself why this cafe is so highly regarded by coffee lovers in the area.

Happy Coffee,
CaffeineThepsadej

user_reviews.Description:
Big Body Coffee is a must-visit for coffee lovers. The café roasts their own beans and offers a variety of specialty beans, both local and international. The coffee is exceptional, and the drip brew was absolutely delicious. Prices are great too—Panama Geisha for just 150 baht and Ethiopia G1 Wash for 100 baht.

For those who appreciate slow bar coffee or are passionate about specialty coffee, this is a spot you shouldn't miss. It’s a small café, but the owner’s dedication and skill really shine through. The café is located in a residential area, so don’t be alarmed when you turn in. You can park right in front of the shop.

user_reviews.text_translated:
YOURMINE Cafe: A hidden gem with delicious coffee.

I actually found them after ordering online. I tried their coffee and it was so good I had to come and try it in person.

The cafe has a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. It's spacious with high ceilings, making it feel comfortable. There are small photo opportunities along the walls, and a nice outdoor seating area.

The drinks are very reasonably priced, especially considering the quality. I hope they maintain this quality and price. They also have pastries, but unfortunately, they seemed to be running low on the day I visited.

This is a great cafe near my home that I'll definitely be back to for a relaxing coffee break.

Oh, and I really appreciate the cafe's generosity. I saw them giving free drinks and snacks to delivery riders when they came to pick up orders. That's something I really admire.

📌Highly recommend! If you're passing by the Kong Sai intersection and want delicious coffee at a great price, stop by. You won't be disappointed.

The restaurant is truly elegant and stylish – definitely one of the nicest places around. The vibe is absolutely 5/5 – calm, elegant, and perfect for a break or meeting with friends.

The food was good, but not amazing. We both ordered pasta – I had lasagna and my partner had spaghetti Alfredo – unfortunately, both dishes were a bit watery, so the taste didn’t quite match the beautiful setting. Still, it wasn’t bad at all, just not as great as we expected from such a luxurious place.

Overall, it’s definitely worth visiting, at least for a coffee and dessert, to enjoy the atmosphere. Highly recommended for the vibe and surroundings.

user_reviews.Description:
At All Café is an absolutely charming coffee shop that offers not just great coffee but an unforgettable experience. The highlight of this delightful spot is the adorable dog, who is both a well-dressed little companion and a beacon of joy for every guest.

As seen in the photo, this sweet pup, donning an irresistibly cute striped outfit, sits at the table with you, providing unparalleled company. While the dog refrains from drinking coffee—wisely avoiding any potential snout-burning mishaps—their presence makes the coffee-sipping experience so much better.

The café itself is warm and welcoming, with a cozy ambiance that pairs perfectly with their delicious drinks. Whether you're a dog lover or simply looking for a unique coffee spot to brighten your day, At All Café is a must-visit. Just don't be surprised if you end up staying longer than planned, captivated by the charm of this furry little host!

user_reviews.Description:
This is my morning go to based on these factors
1. They open at 7am! One of the few that do, so hard to find an early morning g coffee spot until I found this gem.

2. The coffee is delicious, wasn’t a regular coffee drinker…I am now!!!

3. The pastries are fresh baked each morning, I drink my coffee and catch up on assignments and enjoy the procession of amazing baked goods roll out one after another.

4. Last but definitely not least…the owners. They are authentically some of the nicest people you will meet, they exemplify the new generation of business owners who put emphasis on quality and customer service. The husbands makes the coffees and his wife does the pastries, you can taste the pride they pour into their endeavours.

I hope you will read this review and feel compelled to support this standout of a coffee shop and this warm, amazing couple.

The gas station also has restaurants and other shops for you to choose from for meals or purchases, making it a one-stop shop.

✨ Summary
This is a great coffee shop for travelers or those looking for a comfortable place to rest. The quality and atmosphere are up to standard. It's a place you can visit again and again without disappointment.

user_reviews.Description:
I had an incredible time in Chiang Mai, and one of the highlights of my trip was meeting Ankhana, the wonderful owner of Love is Coffee Time. Her cozy café, nestled in the heart of the Umbrella Village in Bor Sang, is a must-visit spot for anyone exploring the area.

Beyond serving great coffee, Ankhana is an inspiring biker girl who also organizes thrilling bike tours. Her generosity, warmth, and hospitality made my experience in Chiang Mai even more special. If you’re ever in the city, make sure to stop by Love is Coffee Time—you won’t regret it!

user_reviews.Description:
Updated: we are back here again to enjoy good food. The farm is back up after the floods. Really good and affordable food and drinks here. We have tried several dishes here from our many trips and its all good.

--------------------------
Making our rounds supporting flooded f&b shops  and we are here is Srisombat Farm. It's quite a car ride deep into Saraphi so you may wanna use the 121 instead of the village roads to get here unless you prefer the small windy roads 😊

The owner and chef is a bubbly character and my wife had a long conversation with him while he prepared our food.

His farm produce was destroyed so he said sorry for not provided any farm fresh vegetables to go with our dishes that he would normally do.

His food is simple but good and tasty. I had the prik prao fried rice which caught my eye as I don't remember trying this dish anywhere. He cooks this very well , not spicy but lots of flavour.

Wife had pad Krapow and this was good too.

He gave us loyalty cards where you can get a free drink after completing the stamps in the card.

Looking forward to visit again when his farm is back in action

Parking : within compound

user_reviews.Description:
Review for On the Way Cafe, Chiang Mai

On a bright and sunny Sunday around noon, I found myself drawn to On the Way Cafe in Chiang Mai. The retro-inspired sign outside caught my eye, promising a unique experience within. As I entered, Sun Rai’s San Francisco Street was playing softly, adding a warm, nostalgic vibe to the sunny atmosphere. The upbeat melody reminded me of lazy Sunday mornings in a foggy coffee shop back in San Francisco—only here, the sunlight streamed through the windows, casting a golden glow across the room.

The cafe itself has a cozy yet vibrant charm, with vintage touches that feel thoughtfully curated. It’s the perfect place to unwind, inviting you to sit back and take in the bright day outside while savoring something delicious.

I opted for their coconut coffee, intrigued by the blend of local flavors. It was fantastic—smooth and creamy, with just the right hint of coconut that brought a refreshing twist without overpowering the coffee. The drink felt like a mini-vacation in itself, blending the comforting richness of coffee with a touch of tropical escape.

On the Way Cafe captures that ideal balance between nostalgia and novelty. Whether you’re reminiscing about foggy mornings in San Francisco or enjoying the sunny charm of Chiang Mai, this little gem provides a welcoming spot to pause, reflect, and savor the moment. It’s a must-visit for anyone looking to experience a taste of creativity and warmth on a beautiful, sunlit day in Chiang Mai.

No one died
I'll live to drink coffee and eat fresh pastries again, just maybe not here

user_reviews.Description:
Where to begin? In 14 years of traveling internationally, Chaiyee Coffee must be the worst experience I have had at a guesthouse.

The owner of Chaiyee Coffee would not stop harassing me in person and over the phone, so I actually had to ask the police to get involved and facilitate me packing and safely leaving the place.

- [ ] Luckily, most guests do not have to deal with the landlord as it is a self-check in place. Unfortunately, one of the rooms I booked started rattling like the engine room on a boat for hours on our first night! It was so loud and shaky from some machine next door, and since it kept going, I had to contact the landlord. He contacted the place next door and basically said, you’ll just have to wait until they close next door. He wanted us to wait it out. It wasn’t until my friend who was staying in the room got upset that the owner agreed to move us to a quiet room downstairs.

However, after we agreed to change rooms, the landlord kept contacting me and asking to talk more. I decided to leave right away and asked the police to come to facilitate communications with the landlord who became aggressive when I didn’t want to talk more about it.

The police officer was very nice and reassured me that the owner would give me a full refund. However, since leaving and contacting the owner through bookings and customer support, no refund has been made.

I do not recommend taking the risk on this place. There are so so many great accommodation options, and great budget options, in Chiang Mai (I have been here about 10 times). Please don’t waste your money or time here. Also, the rooms have bad lighting and no windows. Not a nice setting.

user_reviews.Description:
Excellent Stay at Chaiyee Coffee!

My stay at Chaiyee Coffee was excellent. I stayed here for about two and half weeks and really don't have anything to complain. The location is perfect, within walking distance of many food markets and just few mins from the famous Sunday Night Market at Thaphae Gate.

The accommodation itself is very clean and well-maintained. I really appreciated the comfortable bed, reliable WiFi, and handy basic kitchen utilities. The owner, Winn, ensured a smooth check-in with clear instructions, and amenities like free towels and room service were great touches.

While it's next to a main road and can be a little noisy in the evening, the sound subsides quickly and was never very disruptive. The shared bathroom was kept very neat.

I highly recommend Chaiyee Coffee for a convenient, comfortable, and well-hosted stay in Chiang Mai!

user_reviews.text_translated: After a month's absence, I discovered this new restaurant online right after I came back. It's about a 20-minute drive from the city center, and today was a perfect day for a visit, as the weather was clear. There's ample outdoor parking, and dining is done on a large lawn. user_reviews.Description:
"During my trip to Chiang Mai, I paid a visit to Boon Homestay — and it was one of the highlights of my journey. I'm exploring the area as a possible retirement destination, and my time at Boon gave me a genuine taste of the life I'd love to live.

What makes Boon special is the community. Even as a day visitor, I found myself meeting and making friends from all over the world, hanging out in a chill garden that feels like a home. You're never lonely or homesick in a place like this. The food is inexpensive, home-cooked, and absolutely delicious — the kind of meals that nourish both body and soul.

They also have well-maintained bikes available for rent, which is a perfect way to explore the San Kamphaeng countryside. Everything is properly taken care of with clear safety measures, so you can ride easy and enjoy the scenery.

If you want a carefree, welcoming spot to experience real Chiang Mai living — whether for a meal, a conversation, or just a peaceful afternoon — Boon is the place. I'll definitely be back."

user_reviews.Description:
Great toy play space for kids! The selection of toys here is incredibly comprehensive, stocked mostly with high-quality Melissa & Doug items. They have full pretend kitchen sets, complete doctor play kits, a wide collection of Barbie dolls, Lego bricks, toy cars and various board games—kids can easily spend hours exploring and playing.

Pricing options: 150 THB per hour, and a membership package of 20 hours for 2400 THB. The venue is usually not crowded, which is a big plus, no fighting over toys.

A couple of downsides to note: there is staff shortage at the moment, and there is no discounted package available for stays of 3–4 hours. Overall still a wonderful indoor spot for children to play when visiting Chiang Mai!

user_reviews.text_translated: The shop is located in Ban Thawai, near the canal. It's easily noticeable with a sign. The shop has a small, minimalist style and importantly, it opens early in the morning. The menu includes both coffee and non-coffee drinks. Parking is available along the street in front of the shop.

It seems to me that people come here to work, but the coffee shop/work space has untapped, even wasted potential:

- The chairs are uncomfortable. I came with my partner and we wanted to sit opposite each other, but one of us had to sit on a bench... It was impossible to stay there for several hours.
- I had problems with the connection. Are some sites restricted? (Like TikTok?)

My comment is sincere feedback for this place, which I think has good potential. That's why I'm still giving it 4 stars.

“White shirt now red, my bloody nose
Sleepin', you're on your tippy toes
Creepin' around like no one knows…”

Can’t speak Thai? That’s okay, you speak coffee and so do they. There are drink choices to be made, seating choices, a curious plant looking to grow through the ceiling and a guitar on the wall.

I am not completely comfortable with the way she spells her name but the speakers sound okay to these ears.

Have a visit. You know, give it a try. Good guy.

We ordered a grilled chicken breast salad with roasted sesame (white sesame) dressing. Overall, we thought the price was very good and affordable. As for the food: the chicken breast wasn't too tough, the vegetables were very crisp, and the dressing was delicious.

title: 236 Home Cafe
address: V47M+HJQ 236 Home Cafe, Choeng Doi, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
Great authentic Thai restaurant in Doi Saket.
The food tastes truly local and authentic. The chef is excellent. Fantastic homemade cookies and the hot pan dishes are amazing and served sizzling. The restaurant is clean and comfortable, and I really appreciate that it’s a non-smoking place. Highly recommended for anyone looking for real Thai flavors in Doi Saket.

user_reviews.Description:
A great new addition to Doi Saket. Very thoughtfuly constructed building with a very nice, comfortable and relaxed atmosphere. Nice two level air-conditioned Cafe during the day that doubles as a nice bar after 5pm selling both imported beers, Hoegarden, Budweiser and Heineken plus local beers in the adjoining very clean restaurant. The staff here are extremely courteous and friendly as is the owner. I've only had coffee here and didn't realise there was an adjoining restaurant under the same roof serving Thai food at very good prices and prepared by a very experienced Chef. I'm looking forward to try the food on my return visit and I think I will be impressed. From first impressions I believe this place will be very successful and again a much welcomed addition to Doi Saket. #Edit. I have since tried the excellent food here and it is very good.
Menu both in English and Thai. Menu has been expanded recently and also now offering a variety of nice hot snack foods. Chicken wings etc..

user_reviews.Description:
Wonderful restaurant and cofffee shop just outside of Doi Saket (Choeng Doi technically) on the Borsang road #1014.

Many food choices.  I can heartily recommend the chicken and French fry plate.  The brown pepper sauce is most delicious.  The mixed vegetables not so much (right out of a Makro frozen veggie bag I expect).  But the excellent chicken more than offsets it.  And, unlike any Thai restaurant I’ve been to, this chicken comes deboned.  Juicy and tasty.

Many Thai dishes, and not just the old standbys.

The coffee shop is next door to the restaurant and it looks like some marvelous choices too.

Easy parking.  And they even have an EV charger in the parking area.

Definitely worth a stop.

complete_address.street: บ้านน้ำโจ้, 94/1

user_reviews.Description:
A hidden gem with the warmest hospitality! ☕️🌧️
Walked 22 minutes in the rain just to get here, and it was worth every single step!
As soon as I arrived, I was welcomed by the owner's brother and his super friendly Labrador dog 🐾. Hearing about my rainy walk, he kindly treated me to a warm cup of cocoa on the house! His wife and he are such funny, welcoming, and lovely people.
Why you’ll love it here:
Vegan-friendly: They have plant-based options like oat milk, and the hot cocoa on oat milk was absolutely delicious!
Amazing atmosphere: Beautiful rooftop terrace right under a tree canopy and even a super cute treehouse seating area.
Convenient: Spacious parking available.
I felt so happy and cozy here. Highly recommend this place for great drinks, wholesome vibes, and kind souls! ❤️

user_reviews.Description:
I visited this café two times, and I had a great experience. The place is clean, with relaxing jazz music playing in the background. The drinks are reasonably priced, with a variety of options, including coffee, tea, and soda. You can also customize the sweetness level and add extras like honey if you prefer. They also offer free Wi-Fi and charging spots, which is super convenient.

I had a chat with the owner, who was incredibly friendly. They mentioned that the café opened just a few months ago and that they’re planning to introduce a new menu soon. On my first visit, I ordered a Cocoa Latte with regular sweetness. It was delicious! The owner also gave me a banana cake with caramel to try for free, saying they were still perfecting the recipe. It was fantastic!

The next day, I decided to visit again in the late evening and stayed until the place was about to close. One of the owners remembered me and asked if I wanted to try an unreleased drink, a strawberry latte. The day before, I had asked if they had any fruity drinks besides peach since I’m not a big fan of peach, and they told me the strawberry latte would be available the next day. So, of course, I came back.

The drink was great, but at first, they gave me a regular straw, which made it a bit difficult to mix the strawberry with the milk and drink it properly. When the owner asked for my feedback, I mentioned that the straw wasn’t strong enough for mixing and wasn’t wide enough for the strawberry pulp to pass through. She immediately apologized and brought me a larger straw, the kind used for bubble tea. On top of that, she gave me another banana cake on the house.

I’ll definitely be back if I visit this city again!

user_reviews.Description:
We stopped by this small local café on our way to the football grounds and had a lovely experience. The cappuccino and cacao were delightful, and the chicken sandwich with avocado salad was tasty and fresh under reasonable price expectations.

The café has limited seating, so big groups may find it a bit cramped, and sitting outdoors without ventilation can get warm. The menu isn’t extensive, but everything is made to order, not premade, so there’s a short wait — definitely worth it for the quality.

The café is run by a sweet lady, Teng, who adds a personal touch to the experience with her genuine smile.

Verdict: Great for a cozy stop for coffee and light meals; fresh, well-prepared food and a welcoming vibe.

The café has limited seating, so big groups may find it a bit cramped, and sitting outdoors without ventilation can get warm. The menu isn’t extensive, but everything is made to order, not premade, so there’s a short wait — definitely worth it for the quality.

The café is run by a sweet lady, Teng, who adds a personal touch to the experience with her genuine smile.

Verdict: Great for a cozy stop for coffee and light meals; fresh, well-prepared food and a welcoming vibe.

The **Honey process coffee** is a standout—perfect for making cold brew, which turns out incredibly delicious.

What makes the visit even more special is the owner, an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging lady who provides deep insights into the world of coffee. She’s a pleasure to talk to and shares fascinating stories about coffee. Impressively, she’s one of the pioneers of coffee in the **Thepsadej** region. If you’re passionate about coffee, this is an absolute must-visit destination!

This is a simple, tidy place, the seats are a bit hard, but that is to be expected I think with a simple neighborhood cafe catering mostly to Thais who aren't expecting padded seats.  I think the price was 280 baht, which I found very reasonable.

I can easily recommend At Home, at least for the pizza and coffee.  I don't think you can find pizza this good in a lot of places in Saraphi.

Next time I'm here I'll have some pasta an update my review.

user_reviews.Description:
There is something wonderfully intimate about this cafe. The combination of weathered brick walls, aged wood, warm ambient lighting and an abundance of greenery gives the space a rustic, almost secret garden character. The glass roof brings in soft natural light, while the plants seem to spill into every corner, making you feel as though you’re sitting inside a little botanical sanctuary.

This is the kind of place where you can settle into a quiet corner with a cup of coffee and simply let time slow down. There’s a nostalgic charm here too, with vintage furniture, old-world textures and little decorative details that make the space feel more like someone’s well loved home than a commercial cafe.

A cosy hideaway where coffee, greenery and old world charm come together..quiet, warm and inviting, with just the right touch of rustic soul.

user_reviews.Description:
คาเฟ่ลับหลัง ม.แม่โจ้: มุมถ่ายรูปปัง เครื่องดื่มเลิศ ขนมอร่อยจนต้องแสงออกปาก! ✨
ใครที่กำลังมองหาคาเฟ่ชิลล์ๆ บรรยากาศดี บรรยากาศเงียบสงบ แถวหลังมหาวิทยาลัยแม่โจ้ ห้ามพลาดร้านนี้เด็ดขาด! บอกเลยว่าครบเครื่อง ทั้งเรื่องวิว เครื่องดื่ม และขนม
🌿 บรรยากาศและมุมถ่ายรูป 📸
จุดเด่นแรกที่สัมผัสได้คือบรรยากาศภายในร้านที่ตกแต่งอย่างมีสไตล์ มีความเขียวขจีของต้นไม้ผสมผสานกับเฟอร์นิเจอร์ไม้โทนอบอุ่น ทำให้รู้สึกผ่อนคลายตั้งแต่ก้าวแรกที่เข้ามา มุมถ่ายรูปเยอะมาก! ไม่ว่าจะหันไปทางไหนก็ดูดีไปหมด สายคอนเทนต์ สายถ่ายรูปเล่น รับรองว่าได้รูปสวยๆ อัปลงโซเชียลกันรัวๆ แน่นอน
☕ เครื่องดื่มและ☕ กาแฟ 🥛 นม 🍵 มัจฉะ
มาถึงเรื่องสำคัญอย่างเครื่องดื่มกันบ้าง ร้านนี้เค้าทำเครื่องดื่มได้ออกมาหน้าตาน่าทานมาก และรสชาติก็ดีเยี่ยมไม่แพ้หน้าตาเลย
กาแฟ (Coffee): หอม เข้มข้น กลมกล่อม คอกาแฟต้องถูกใจ
นม (Milk): นมสดแท้ หอมมัน นุ่มละมุนลิ้น
มัจฉะ (Matcha): เข้มข้น หอมกลิ่นชาเขียวมัจฉะแท้ๆ ไม่ขมเกินไป
🍰 ขนมและของหวาน 🍩
ปิดท้ายด้วยของหวานที่ต้องบอกว่าอร่อยสุดๆ จริงๆ! ทางร้านมีขนมให้เลือกหลายอย่าง ทั้งเค้ก พาย คุกกี้ ทุกอย่างหน้าตาน่าทานมาก และรสชาติก็อร่อยมากเช่นกัน เค้กเนื้อนุ่ม หวานพอดีๆ ไม่เลี่ยนจนเกินไป ส่วนพายก็แป้งกรอบ ไส้แน่น คุกกี้ก็ชิ้นใหญ่ หอมอร่อย
📍 พิกัด 🗺️
ร้านตั้งอยู่หลัง ม.แม่โจ้ หาไม่ยากเลยครับ สามารถขับรถตาม Google Maps มาได้เลย
สรุป 👍
หากใครกำลังหาคาเฟ่แถว ม.แม่โจ้ ที่มีครบทั้งบรรยากาศดี มุมถ่ายรูปสวย เครื่องดื่มรสชาติเยี่ยม และขนมอร่อยถูกใจ แนะนำร้านนี้เลยครับ รับรองว่าไม่ผิดหวังแน่นอน!

user_reviews.text_translated:
Hidden Cafe Behind Maejo University: Amazing Photo Spots, Delicious Drinks, and Desserts That Will Make You Smile! ✨
If you're looking for a chill cafe with a great atmosphere and a quiet setting behind Maejo University, you absolutely can't miss this place! It has everything: amazing views, delicious drinks, and tasty desserts.
🌿 Atmosphere and Photo Spots 📸
The first thing you'll notice is the stylish interior design. The lush greenery of the plants blends with warm-toned wooden furniture, creating a relaxing feeling from the moment you step inside. There are so many photo opportunities! Everywhere you look is perfect. Content creators and photography enthusiasts are guaranteed to get stunning photos to upload to social media non-stop.
☕ Drinks and ☕ Coffee 🥛 Milk 🍵 Matcha
Now, let's talk about the drinks. This cafe makes drinks that are incredibly visually appealing. And the taste is as excellent as the appearance!
Coffee: Fragrant, rich, and smooth. Coffee lovers will definitely like it.
Milk: Real fresh milk, fragrant, creamy, and smooth on the palate.
Matcha: Rich, with the fragrant aroma of real matcha green tea, not too bitter.
🍰 Desserts and Sweets 🍩
Finally, the desserts are absolutely delicious! The shop has many options to choose from, including cakes, pies, and cookies. Everything looks very appetizing, and the taste is delicious as well. The cakes are soft, just the right amount of sweetness, not too cloying. The pies have a crispy crust and a generous filling. The cookies are large, fragrant, and delicious.
📍 Location 🗺️
The shop is located behind Maejo University. It's easy to find. You can drive there using Google Maps.
Summary 👍
If you're looking for a cafe near Maejo University that has everything: a great atmosphere, beautiful photo spots, excellent drinks, and delicious desserts, I highly recommend this shop. You won't be disappointed!

user_reviews.Description:
Slow Bar ZapaCoffee: A Hidden Gem in Chiang Mai for the True Coffee Lover

Stepping into Slow Bar ZapaCoffee felt like discovering a secret handshake among coffee enthusiasts. It’s not just a coffee shop; it’s an experience, a quiet rebellion against the ordinary, nestled perfectly within Chiang Mai’s vibrant walking street. Forget what you thought you knew about night markets; this place alone makes you rethink your entire itinerary.

My journey began with SOPA’S ESTATE medium roast, and I just had to try it both as a hot drip and a cold brew. The distinct character of Mrs. Sopa’s farm truly shines through, a testament to exceptional beans and masterful preparation. Each sip told a story, a delightful narrative of unique flavors that lingered long after the cup was empty. It was an absolute standout.

For my take-away adventures, I indulged in a few more cold drip delights: the robust CHIANG RAI Medium roast, the intriguing HEPSADEJ, and the beautifully balanced APA House Blend ETHIOPIA. Each one was a perfect companion for exploring the charming streets, a liquid treasure to savor.

What truly elevates ZapaCoffee, however, are the people behind the bar. The baristas, both the kind gentleman and the lovely lady, are not just skilled; they are genuinely passionate, knowledgeable, and incredibly welcoming. Watching their meticulous drip technique was a masterclass in itself – so much so that I’m inspired to try and replicate their artistry at home! Their friendly demeanor and willingness to share their expertise made the experience all the more enriching.

But beyond the beans and the brilliant baristas, it’s the philosophy that truly resonated with me: late-night coffee dripping. There’s something profoundly touching about enjoying such a carefully crafted brew as the city winds down. It’s a moment of quiet contemplation, a perfect end to a day, or perhaps, the start of a reflective evening. This unique approach is what makes ZapaCoffee an absolute must-visit.

For any coffee aficionado venturing into Chiang Mai, Slow Bar ZapaCoffee is an undeniable hidden gem. It’s a place where every detail is considered, every bean respected, and every cup poured with passion. Trust me, once you’ve experienced the magic here, you won’t want to go back to your old walking street haunts. This is the new standard.

user_reviews.text_translated: On March 26, 1969, I ordered a drink for 60฿ and paid via credit card. However, the employee somehow charged my card twice. My credit card app showed one charge, and then another. I contacted the employee about this, and they said the system only processed one transaction. They also said if the card wasn't charged the next day, I could contact the store for a refund. However, since I live far away and am not from the area, I asked for their LINE contact information. Today, I contacted the store to request a refund, but I haven't received any response. This is urgent and needs immediate attention. I bought just one drink for 60฿, but now I have to pay 120฿. This is unacceptable. Every baht counts. I urge management to address this issue.

address: No.98 Sunpaka, Doisaket Rd, Pa Pong, Doi Saket District, Chiang Mai 50220

user_reviews.Description:
I found this place by chance while looking for somewhere new to eat in the Doi Saket area, and it turned out to be a wonderful surprise.

It’s a small farmstay with a restaurant, and I honestly didn’t come with big expectations, but the food was excellent. They use fresh ingredients from their own garden, and you can really taste the difference. Everything felt fresh, homemade, and prepared with care.

We ordered pizza, salad, and a fruit dessert. The pizza had a soft, delicious crust, and the toppings were full of flavor. The salad was simple but very high quality, with ingredients that tasted like they came straight from the garden. The fruit dessert with homemade yogurt was the perfect way to finish the meal.

What made the evening even more special was the atmosphere. The host invited us to join a shared table, and we ended up having a great evening talking with interesting people. It felt warm, relaxed, and very personal.

Great food, lovely concept, and a fun, welcoming atmosphere. Highly recommended. Thank you — we’ll definitely be back.

The atmosphere is friendly and inspiring, and you can really feel the teacher’s passion for coffee. Highly recommend this place to anyone who wants to learn how to make great coffee!

Also after 1Pm you can come and enjoy the good coffee a very nice place for working and drinking a good cup of coffee

user_reviews.Description:
Baan Samadhi feels like a cozy little house nestled in a lush forest, radiating warmth with its cute vintage decor. The banana cream cheese cake was absolutely delicious—so good I had to order two slices because one just wasn’t enough! Tried another cake and a toast dish from the menu, both were  satisfying. The drinks have a slow-bar vibe, perfect for unwinding. The chill atmosphere and natural surroundings make it a refreshing escape.
Little Samadhi, the owner’s daughter, is absolutely adorable and served the desserts herself. Plus, there’s a friendly cat named Santi (peace) who warmly greets the guests. If you’re in the area, you’ve got to stop by this lovely cafe.

user_reviews.text_translated: This restaurant, nestled atop a mountain, is a rare find during your travels. Their signature herbal tea is refreshingly sweet, and their coffee is rich and aromatic – truly exceptional, yet surprisingly affordable, averaging less than 100 baht per person. The owner is warm and attentive, providing thoughtful service; they even carefully kept my bag, which I had inadvertently left behind – a truly heartwarming gesture. The restaurant boasts a comfortable and relaxing atmosphere, with ample free parking, making it perfect for a short break after a long drive. While there is occasional litter and a 5 baht fee for using the restrooms, these minor flaws don't detract from the overall experience. Closed every Monday, this place is definitely worth a special stop if you're passing through. It's a highly cost-effective rest stop and strongly recommended for travelers looking for a break – you won't regret it; it's excellent value for money.

user_reviews.Description: Hidden gem! I found this café by accident. The shop is tucked behind lots of fern plants, so it’s easy to miss, but once you find it, it’s absolutely worth the effort. The coffee is excellent—I loved it from the very first sip. They also use a very rare coffee machine, which was a pleasant surprise. The café isn’t in the city center; it’s located quietly beside the Middle Ring Road (Road 3029), making it a peaceful stop away from the crowds. Highly recommended if you’re in the area.

The staff service is okay, no problems, and service is quick and up to standard.

💻 Shop Atmosphere

🚗 Parking
There is ample parking for customers, and it's not difficult to find a parking spot.
